summary: Audio now runs 0.02% FAST, so the ring overflows and drops ~9 samples a second
description:
Found 4.9 hours into the PIZERO-98 soak, on the post-PIZERO-119 build. The old 0.9% SHORTFALL is gone; the error changed sign.

  producer   48,010 samples/s median against 48,000 asked for = 100.021%
  ring fill  pinned at ~7,850 of 8,192, i.e. nearly full rather than the intended half
  skips      156,528 in 4.9 h, about 8.7 a second, steady
  underruns  0 after the boot transient

A 'skip' is the READER catching up after the producer laps it (coco_machine_audio_read, the avail > AUDIO_RING_SAMPLES branch): samples that were made and then thrown away. At 48 kHz, 8.7/s is 0.018% of the stream discarded in bursts rather than smoothly, so it is not silence but it is not clean either, and it is the most likely remaining contributor to anything audible in PIZERO-41.

WHY IT CHANGED SIGN: emulated time is now paced correctly (the frame fits, PIZERO-119), so the producer runs at the CoCo's true rate. The consumer is paced by the real pixel clock. The two clocks are independent and 0.02% apart, so one of them must give: before the fix the emulator was slow and starved the stream, now it is fractionally fast and overruns it.

THE FIX IS RATE MATCHING, NOT A BIGGER RING: a fixed offset of 0.02% fills any buffer eventually. Options, cheapest first: (a) a slow servo that nudges the resampler's tick budget by a few parts per million to hold the ring near half full, which is what a real audio clock recovery does and needs no new plumbing; (b) drop or duplicate ONE sample when the ring drifts past a threshold, spread out rather than in bursts, which is cheap and inaudible at this rate; (c) derive the sample rate from the pixel clock so the two cannot disagree, which is the correct fix and the largest change.

COMPLETION CONDITION: ring fill holds near half over a multi-hour run, skips per hour in single digits or zero, underruns still zero. Related: PIZERO-41 (audible quality), PIZERO-32 (the sink's clock assumption), PIZERO-40 (pool depth).

[2026-09-18 IMPLEMENTED as option (a), the servo, not yet on hardware (board mid-soak).
lib/coco_machine/src/audio_servo.h holds the control law, header-only and machine-free so the LOOP can be simulated on the host rather than watched for hours. coco_machine calls it once per frame, only after the reader has primed, and the producer's accumulator now uses the servo's rate instead of the constant. The telemetry reports it as srv=, so a drifting clock is visible as a rate rather than inferred from skips after the fact.
WHY PROPORTIONAL-ONLY IS ENOUGH: ring fill is the INTEGRAL of the rate error, so proportional control on fill is integral control on rate. That gives zero steady-state rate error with no integral term and nothing to wind up. The ring settles at a constant OFFSET from centre, and that offset is the correction: K x the mismatch, 32 x ~10 = ~320 samples, 4% of the ring.
TUNING: K=32 (about 32 s to settle) and a clamp of +/-64 samples/s, which is 0.13% or 0.023 of a semitone, inaudible. The clamp exists so a bug elsewhere cannot detune the machine; a test asserts it stays under 0.2%.
TESTED BY SIMULATING THE LOOP over six hours of model time at the measured +0.021%: never within 256 samples of either wall, settles above centre (the sign matters: holding the producer slower REQUIRES a ring above centre), mirror-image behaviour for the opposite sign, recovers from both a full ring (the state the soak is in now, ~7,850) and an empty one, and does not hunt. Also pinned: a 0.9% mismatch, the old PIZERO-119 defect, saturates the clamp and drains the ring rather than pretending to cope, because that is a different bug and should look like one. 84 tests now pass.
Two of the simulation tests failed first time and both were MY sign errors in the expectations, not the servo's.
VERIFY ON HARDWARE: after the soak, watch fill hold near 4,400 and skips stop climbing. The next soak is the real test.]

[2026-09-28 FIRST HARDWARE EVIDENCE for the servo, from a 31 s Space Assault capture after a cartridge cold boot: ring fill rose steadily 3,063 -> 3,916 while the servo rate eased 48,031 -> 48,005 samples/s toward its set-point, prod tracking it (48,036 -> 48,011), under=0/s and skips=0 throughout. That is the behaviour the host simulation predicted (settle above centre, no hunting). Still wanted: a multi-hour run showing fill holding near the set-point and skips staying flat.]

[2026-10-11 CLOSED in the tracker clean-up: the completion condition is met by the PIZERO-168 soak (docs/measurements/logs/2026-10-09-1153-pizero_stream_60-card.log, 26.7 h observed). Over 1,605 one-minute [aud] samples the ring fill held at median 4,356 (min 441 is the boot transient, max 4,394) against the ~4,400 set-point, skips=0 for the whole run, underruns zero after priming. The servo behaves as the host simulation predicted. Whether the audio now SOUNDS right is PIZERO-41, a listening test.]

summary: Lid screw bosses snap off at the tip: web them into the corners, open the pilot to 2.2 mm

summary: BOOT button opens the disk selection overlay, like F12
description:
USER DECISION 2026-09-25: once the firmware is running, pressing BOOT opens the disk selection overlay, the same as F12 (PIZERO-81c). The case has no other buttons, so this gives a machine without a keyboard attached a way in. Split out of PIZERO-116.

HOW THE BUTTON WORKS (docs/RP2350-PiZero-schematic.pdf): BOOT is Key1, pulling QSPI_SS_N (the flash chip select, net USB_BOOT, via 1K) low. Held at reset it enters the USB bootloader; that recovery path is in the boot ROM and nothing here can break it. At runtime it can be read with the standard BOOTSEL trick: float the QSPI_SS pin, sample it, restore it. While floated, NOTHING may fetch from flash (XIP) on either core.

THE RISK, and why this starts with a spike: arduino-pico's BOOTSEL macro makes that safe by idling the other core, but core 1 here drives libdvi scanout and HDMI audio islands. Idling it would glitch the picture and could drop audio sync. The libdvi IRQ and data-island encode are RAM-resident (.time_critical, PIZERO-37), but whether core 1's WHOLE path avoids flash for a few microseconds is not established. Candidate approach: sample from RAM-resident code on core 0 with its interrupts off, at a low rate (every ~50 ms is plenty for a button), and prove core 1 never touches flash in that window, or do the sample from core 1 itself between scanlines.

STEP 1, SPIKE: sample BOOT at a low rate in the product build (pizero_stream_60) and report presses on serial. Run it long enough to show no video dropouts, no audio underruns and no sync loss (the PIZERO-98 soak telemetry measures exactly these). If it cannot be made safe, record why here and close this; F12 stays the only way in.

STEP 2: once PIZERO-81c exists, a debounced BOOT press does whatever F12 does. Pressing it while the overlay is open is a candidate for closing it (like ESC); decide when implementing.

DEPENDS ON: PIZERO-81c for step 2. Step 1 can run any time.

DONE WHEN: on hardware, BOOT opens the overlay with no visible or audible glitch, and BOOT+RUN still enters the bootloader for flashing.

[2026-09-27 DEFERRED by the user: with only one usable button there is not enough to do after it; F12 covers the overlay. Kept on file if a keyboard-less path is ever needed.]

summary: Prove an optimised 6809 core behaves identically to the pristine one
description:
Stage 1 of the CoCo 3 plan, and a precondition for PIZERO-131. Nothing anywhere (this repo or upstream ~/github/xroar) tests 6809 correctness, and PIZERO-131 is about to optimise a core we have treated as trusted and untouched. Build the safety net first.

DO: freeze today's vendored core (lib/xroar_core/src/mc6809/mc6809.c, mc6809_common.c, lib/xroar_core/src/mc680x/mc680x_ops.c and headers) under test/ as the reference. New native suite test/test_mc6809_lockstep/ runs reference and working cores side by side against the same flat 64 KB memory model, recording every bus access (address, read/write, data, NVMA flag) and the registers at every instruction boundary; the first divergence fails with the instruction and cycle. Inputs: (a) seeded random instruction streams covering opcode pages 1 to 3, every indexed and indirect mode, and IRQ/FIRQ/NMI/SYNC/CWAI; (b) optionally a real ROM boot for N million cycles when COCO_ROM_DIR is set, skipped otherwise (the repo ships no ROMs). Follow the [env:native] conventions (platformio.ini: headers by relative path, no Arduino).

DONE WHEN: the suite runs in pio test -e native, passes against an unmodified core, and demonstrably catches a deliberately injected one-cycle or one-flag change.

Plan and reasoning: docs/coco3-plan.md; feasibility numbers: docs/coco3-feasibility.md (PIZERO-111). BUILT 2026-10-09: test/mc6809_reference/ (the core frozen at 8a9032f) and test/test_mc6809_lockstep/ (core_ref.c and core_work.c each compile a whole core under a prefix via renames.h and lockstep_core.inc; one instruction per step through the instruction posthook, a bus-cycle cap for SYNC and HALT; registers and every bus cycle compared). Scenarios: 24 seeded random 64 KB images with a random NMI/FIRQ/IRQ/HALT schedule (15000 steps each), all 256 indexed postbytes through LEAX/LDA/STA, the page 2 and 3 opcode sweep, SYNC/CWAI/SWI/SWI2/SWI3/RTI under driven lines, two comparator self-checks (a flipped C flag, an injected extra bus cycle), and a 3-million-step Color BASIC boot when COCO_ROM_DIR is set (passes with ~/Desktop/coco/roms). Whole native suite 236 pass in 9.5 s. LEFT (file or finish): the manual injection recipe (edit one line of the live core, see it fail) was not yet run; a line in docs/BUILD.md section 5 about running the harness and COCO_ROM_DIR; docs/coco3-plan.md stage 1 to say it exists. DONE 2026-10-09: injection demonstrated on the live core and reverted: op_add not setting H was caught at random seed 1, step 6 (cc F0 vs D0); NOP without its dummy cycle was caught at seed 5, step 7706 and in the page 2/3 sweep ('reference took 2 bus cycles, working 1'). docs/BUILD.md section 5 and docs/coco3-plan.md stage 1 point at the harness. All DONE WHEN conditions met on the host; no hardware involved. PIZERO-131 may start, with PIZERO-130 for the baseline.

summary: Measure the CoCo 2 machine running at 1.79 MHz
description:
Stage 2 of the CoCo 3 plan. A CoCo 3 runs its 6809 at 1.79 MHz, twice the CoCo 2. Running our CoCo 2 machine at twice its cycles per frame reproduces exactly that CPU load, before any GIME cost, so the speed work in PIZERO-131 has a real target and baseline.

DO: new env pizero_cpu179 in platformio.ini extending pizero_stream_60, with a build flag that doubles CYCLES_PER_FRAME (src/main.cpp, 14915 to 29830 at 60 Hz). A real env, never PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS (docs/BUILD.md: it links stale objects). Record cpu= at 1x and 2x with scripts/soak.py record then analyse --kind bench into docs/measurements/. Teach soak.py analyse to print the frame-budget percentage (sum of phases / 16,667 us), which the issues currently work out by hand. Note in docs/BUILD.md.

EXPECTED from docs/coco3-feasibility.md: about 20.8 ms of emulation per frame at 2x, 125% of a frame; today's measured cost is about 180 host clocks per emulated bus cycle.

Plan and reasoning: docs/coco3-plan.md; feasibility numbers: docs/coco3-feasibility.md (PIZERO-111).

[2026-10-11 BUILT, not yet measured on the board. CPU_SPEED_MUL (default 1) multiplies the cycles coco_machine_run_cycles gets each frame (src/main.cpp, beside the CYCLES_PER_FRAME defines); env pizero_cpu179 extends pizero_stream_60 with -DCPU_SPEED_MUL=2, i.e. 29,830 cycles a frame. Both build, RAM 75.8%. BUILD.md env table and flag matrix updated. The whole emulated machine runs twice as fast at 2x (VDG fields, timers, sound), so the audio ring overflows and counts skips: a measurement build only. scripts/soak.py analyse now prints the frame-budget % (median cpu+render+blit+aud over the frame period), emulation alone as %, and host clocks per emulated cycle (cpu median x sysclk / cycles per frame), from an ENV_FRAME table per env; the figures go into the archive record as frame_budget_pct. Checked against the PIZERO-168 soak log: 74.9% of the frame, emulation 64.1%, 180.4 host clocks per cycle, matching docs/coco3-feasibility.md's ~180. NEXT: on a spare board (not the PIZERO-203 soak board), record a few minutes of each build on the same workload with scripts/soak.py record, then analyse --kind bench to archive both.]

[2026-10-12 DONE: both baselines measured on hardware and archived with the git hash (docs/measurements/2026-10.jsonl, kind bench; logs docs/measurements/logs/2026-10-12-0926-pizero_stream_60-unit10.log and 2026-10-12-0930-pizero_cpu179-unit10.log, firmware 8201da2). Unit 10, BASIC prompt after autorun typed DIR with OPIL-EN.dsk in drive 0, keyboard attached, 3 minutes each. 1x: emulation median 10,975 us = 65.8% of the frame, whole frame 78.1%, 60 fps. 2x: emulation 21,947 us = 131.7%, whole frame 144.2%, 42 fps, audio ring overflowing as expected (skips). Both 185.4 host clocks per emulated cycle, so cost is exactly linear in clock rate. The base grew from the 10.4 ms in coco3-feasibility.md, so the overrun is 32%, not 25%. TARGET FOR PIZERO-131: about 105 clocks per cycle (emulation of 29,830 cycles in ~12.5 ms), a 1.77x speed-up. Written into docs/coco3-feasibility.md. Note for the PIZERO-203 soak on the same card: soak-001 is the 1x run and soak-002 the cpu179 run; the soak proper starts at soak-003.]

summary: 6809 emulation about 1.7x faster, so a 1.79 MHz machine fits in a frame
description:
Stage 3 of the CoCo 3 plan: the experiment the whole CoCo 3 effort hangs on. Target about 105 host clocks per emulated bus cycle (from about 180), so 29,830 cycles a frame fit in about 12.5 ms. Also gives the CoCo 2 product build more headroom.

HOT SPOTS FOUND (2026-09-26 research): every bus cycle including dummy NVMA cycles (NVMA_CYCLE = peek_byte(cpu, 0xffff), mc6809_common.c:96, up to 5 per indexed EA) is an out-of-line call into coco_mem_cycle (coco_machine.cpp:427-599), in another translation unit so never inlined; per access it repeats a two-stage decode, total_mem_cycles++, an event-head check, audio_integrate(16), an IRQ dirty check and cycles_remaining -= 16, and the CPU stores 3 interrupt latches (mc6809_common.c:60-93); op_sub, op_sub16, op_add16 and word_immediate from mc680x_ops.c landed in FLASH behind veneers from the RAM-resident mc6809_run.

ORDER, cheapest and safest first, stop when the pizero_cpu179 build fits: (1) ALU helpers to RAM (HOT_FUNC in lib/xroar_core/src/hot.h, or inline); (2) NVMA cycles advance time without decode or ROM read; (3) inline page-table fast path for RAM/ROM, only I/O and SAM writes via coco_mem_cycle; (4) batched bookkeeping: cached next-event tick, audio integrated in spans (host test for identical samples), one cycle check per instruction; (5) only if still short: table or computed-goto dispatch, or one translation unit.

EVERY STEP: PIZERO-129 lockstep passes, all native tests pass, pizero_cpu179 measured and logged, product build soak unchanged.

GATE: full speed, go to PIZERO-133; about 80% or better, go with the PIZERO-135 audio policy; well short, stop and record why in docs/coco3-feasibility.md.

DEPENDS ON: PIZERO-129, PIZERO-130.

Plan and reasoning: docs/coco3-plan.md; feasibility numbers: docs/coco3-feasibility.md (PIZERO-111).

[2026-10-12 BASELINE from PIZERO-130 (2026-10-12): 185.4 host clocks per emulated cycle at both 1x and 2x on unit 10 (emulation 10,975 us at 14,915 cycles; 21,947 us at 29,830). The target of ~105 clocks per cycle is a 1.77x speed-up. Measure each step with pizero_cpu179 and scripts/soak.py analyse --kind bench, which now prints clocks per cycle directly; use the same workload (BASIC prompt after autorun DIR) so steps compare.]

[2026-10-12 REVISED PLAN from PIZERO-209's measurement. The time is in the bus path (~150 of 185 clocks per cycle), not the 6809 core (~35), so this is plumbing, not a core rewrite; step 5 (dispatch rewrite) is unlikely to be needed and the core's own share cannot deliver 80 clocks anyway. Estimates per emulated cycle, to be measured step by step with pizero_cpu179 and pizero_cpuprof_hook:
(a) Dummy cycles (36.5%) skip decode and data and touch no memory: their decode+data share is ~57 raw, so perhaps 15-20 saved overall. Worth far more than first estimated.
(b) IRQ lines and the cycle budget checked once per instruction (4.05 cycles) instead of every cycle: irq+budget is ~26 raw, so perhaps 15-19 saved. Needs care: interrupt latches are sampled per cycle, so check against PIZERO-129 lockstep and the PIA timing.
(c) Events and audio, the biggest section (~56 raw): split it first (queue check, event dispatch such as VDG scanline work, audio_integrate and its per-sample work). The queue check and audio can be batched per instruction; the dispatch is real work and stays. Perhaps 20-35 saved, the least certain.
(d) RAM/ROM fast path inlined into the core, hardware addresses only through the hook: removes call, return and the latch stores for most accesses, ~10-16.
(e) The ALU helpers op_sub, op_sub16, op_add16 and word_immediate are in flash in the product build (seen with nm): move to RAM, cheap and safe, gain unknown.
SUM of the estimates: roughly 60-90 clocks, so 105 (from 185) is plausible but not assured; (c) decides it. Order by safety and certainty: (e), (a), (d), then split and attack (c), then (b).]

[2026-10-12 STEP (e) DONE, gain about nil. nm on pizero_stream_60 found 17 functions the RAM-resident run loop called in flash, not 4: op_sub, op_sub16, op_add16, word_immediate, word_direct, word_extended, word_indexed (the last three carry the bus calls inside them), branch_condition (every Bcc), push_irq_registers, take_interrupt (mc6809.c), mc6821_set_cx1, mc6821_update_cx2_state, write_cr (mc6821.c), vcounter_update, update_from_register (mc6883.c), event_queue, event_dequeue (events.c). All now HOT_FUNC; no RAM-to-flash veneer is left on the emulation path except csg_bus_write and gime_timer_restart (rare writes, left in flash) and two USB hooks. Cost 2.7 KB RAM (product 76.3%). Measured A/B on the second board C58D06257AE30E85 (not in the QC log), pizero_cpu179, same boot workload, about 4 min each: emulation 21,377 -> 21,311 us a frame, 180.6 -> 180.0 host clocks per cycle, 0.3%. So the 16 KB XIP cache was already holding these; kept anyway because the hot path no longer depends on that cache, which the CoCo 3's extra code will compete for. Logs: docs/measurements/logs/2026-10-12-1803-pizero_cpu179-C58D06257AE30E85.log (before) and 2026-10-12-1809-... (after). Note this board's baseline is 180.6, unit 10's 185.4: compare steps on one board only.
Side effects: pizero_wavmeas (the last double-buffered env, ~99% RAM) overflowed by 2,068 bytes; on the user's call it is now single-buffered via the new FB_SINGLE flag (73%), so no env is a near-full canary any more (BUILD.md, pipeline.md, CLAUDE.md updated). soak.py analyse now takes the env from the LOGGER START line when the log has no boot banner (it had fallen back to pizero_stream_60 and printed 361 clocks per cycle).
NEXT: (a) the dummy-cycle fast path, measured the same way on C58D06257AE30E85.]

[2026-10-12 STEP (a) DONE: 180.0 -> 165.8 host clocks per cycle (emulation 21,311 -> 19,628 us a frame at 2x, fps 43 -> 47), 14.2 clocks, 7.9%. NVMA_CYCLE (mc6809_common.c) now calls nvma_cycle(), which samples the interrupt latches as before and calls the new coco_mem_nvma (coco_machine.cpp): it sets what the full decode of a $FFFF read would (sam->S = 2, D = rom[$3FFF]) and goes straight to mem_cycle_tail, the per-cycle events, audio, IRQ and budget work now shared with coco_mem_cycle. The lockstep harness gives the live core a mem_nvma that records the same $FFFF read, so test_mc6809_lockstep still compares it cycle for cycle; all 237 host tests pass, including test_color_basic_boot with COCO_ROM_DIR=~/Desktop/coco/roms.
TRAP FOUND: the first build measured 195.8 (9% SLOWER). With two callers, audio_integrate stopped being inlined and landed in flash, so every cycle crossed into flash. Fixed with always_inline. After every step, check nm for a RAM-to-flash veneer on the hot path before measuring. Log of the slow build: docs/measurements/logs/2026-10-12-1845-...; the good one: 2026-10-12-1931-....
NEXT: (d) inline RAM/ROM fast path into the core, measured the same way. Progress table in docs/coco3-feasibility.md.]

[2026-10-12 STEP (d) DONE: 165.8 -> 156.6 host clocks per cycle (emulation 19,628 -> 18,534 us at 2x, 47 -> 49 fps), 9.2 clocks, under the 10-16 estimate because each cycle still calls coco_mem_tick for the tail. New lib/xroar_core/include/coco_fastbus.h: struct coco_fastbus {ram, rom, cart, ram_top, rom_top, cart_top, cart_mask}, owned by coco_machine.cpp and kept current by fastbus_sync() at init, on SAM TY writes ($FFDE/$FFDF), on GMC bank switches, on cart install and on cold reset. fetch_byte_notrace and store_byte (mc6809_common.c) move RAM/ROM/cart bytes themselves and call coco_mem_tick (the shared tail); everything else, I/O and SAM registers, still takes coco_mem_cycle. In all-RAM mode ram_top is $FF00. The lockstep harness sets ram_top to its ROM base and records coco_mem_tick cycles the same way, so random streams, sweeps and the Color BASIC boot still compare cycle for cycle; its ROM and cart windows are empty, so the product's ROM and cartridge windows are checked by review only (they copy the hook's case 1-3 expressions).
PLACEMENT: the bigger bus helpers stopped being inlined and fell into flash, then fetch_byte, fetch_word_notrace and byte_immediate did. CPU_PROF_INLINE is now always_inline in every build; fetch_word, fetch_word_notrace and the operand fetches (byte_immediate/direct/extended/indexed, short_relative) are HOT_FUNC. RAM +3.5 KB (product 77.1%, cpuprof 78.5%).
HARDWARE CHECK OWED (bench board has no screen or keyboard): a cartridge game, a banked cart if one turns up, and NitrOS-9, which runs in all-RAM mode, on the product build.
NEXT: split (c) events+audio with pizero_cpuprof_hook, then batch.]

[2026-10-12 HARDWARE CHECK of step (d) passed: product build (904e014) on the bench board C58D06257AE30E85, now with a keyboard and monitor. The user ran a cartridge (F10, Dungeons of Daggorath), NitrOS-9 from NOS9L1.DSK (all-RAM mode) and disk games: "everything is ok so far". Product emulation on that board is 9.4 ms a frame at 1x, down from 11.1 ms before PIZERO-131.]

[2026-10-13 STEP (c) BUILT, NOT YET CLEANLY MEASURED. Instead of trimming the per-cycle tail, most cycles now skip it. coco_fastbus.deadline is the earliest event tick at which a cycle needs the tail: the end of the 16-tick access that crosses the next audio sample boundary, the next event, the end of the run's budget, or now when the interrupt lines are dirty at run start. Before it, a RAM/ROM/cart or dummy cycle only does event_current_tick += 16 inline in the core (coco_fastbus_advance), with no call. The audio for skipped cycles is caught up in one span (audio_catch_up) at the start of every tail, at the hook's entry (before a PIA1 write can change the level) and at the end of each run (before the servo changes the rate). The budget is now an end tick (g_budget_end) instead of cycles_remaining. The integrator moved to lib/coco_machine/src/audio_integ.h; new test/test_audio_integ runs per-access integration against span skip-ahead over random streams (level changes, odd-length accesses, servo rate changes per frame) and requires identical samples; a deliberate off-by-one in the boundary count fails 3 of its 4 tests. The test models the machine's catch-up placement rather than running coco_machine.cpp. The lockstep harness keeps its deadline at 0, so every cycle still goes through its recorder. 241 host tests pass. MEASUREMENT: the one bench run (docs/measurements/logs/2026-10-12-2325-...) was contaminated: 7 s at the BASIC prompt at about 12.2 ms emulation a frame at 2x (about 103 clocks per cycle, against 156.6 after (d)), then a graphics game ran flat out. That is the one thing left before closing.] [2026-10-13 CLOSED. The user played Dungeons of Daggorath on the product build (pizero_stream_60, 4cc400b) and reported the sound right, so step (c)'s audio change is inaudible; step (d) was checked on hardware earlier (cartridge, NitrOS-9, disk games). summary: SAM double speed (POKE 65495) is never applied: every access costs 16 ticks
description:
Found 2026-09-26 while researching PIZERO-131. coco_machine_run_cycles budgets cycles*16 ticks and the fast path in coco_mem_cycle hardcodes ncycles = 16 (lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp:455, 481), so a guest that sets the SAM rate bits for double or address-dependent speed runs at normal speed. docs/cpu-speed.md says fast cycles cost 8 ticks; that is wrong for this code and its line references are stale.

CAUTION: fixing it lets a guest demand up to twice the CPU work per frame and overrun (docs/cpu-speed.md estimates about 18.8 ms), which is what PIZERO-48's cap exists for. Fix together with that decision, not alone, and correct docs/cpu-speed.md at the same time.

DONE WHEN: POKE 65495,0 measurably speeds up a BASIC loop on hardware (or is deliberately capped per PIZERO-48 and documented), and cpu-speed.md matches the code.

[2026-10-14 IMPLEMENTED, awaiting the user's hardware check] At the user's request ("let's enable double speed poke for the coco2 also"; normal speed by default, the POKE must work). sam_ticks (lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp) gives each CoCo 2 cycle 8 or 16 ticks from the SAM rate, mc6883.c's fast_cycle rule: fast when R1 is set, or R = 1 and the cycle is neither RAM nor PIA0. g_m.sam_r shadows R from writes to $FFD6-$FFD9 and is cleared on reset. struct coco_fastbus (lib/xroar_core/include/coco_fastbus.h) now has ticks (RAM window) and rom_ticks (ROM, cartridge, dummy cycles), set by fastbus_sync; coco_fastbus_advance and COCO_TICK (mc6809_common.c) take the length. A paged CoCo 2 maps ROM pages only when the two agree. The audio catch-up integrates in 8-tick steps on the CoCo 2, exact at a steady level for mixed 8/16 runs (new host test test_mixed_lengths_caught_up_in_eights; 255 tests pass). Not modelled: the SAM's 15/17/25-tick rate-transition cycles. Measured on hardware (new board, pizero_fdctrace, a 3000-iteration BASIC FOR loop): 188 jiffies normal, 116 at POKE 65495 (1.62x), 94 at POKE 65497 (2.00x). pizero_stream_60 emulation: 6.2 ms normal (6.1 before the change), 12.4 ms at 65495, 12.6 ms at 65497, late 0, audio short 0.0%. RAM pizero_stream_60 419,364 -> 421,376 bytes (80.4%). A first reading of 12.5 ms at the OK prompt was the user's CoCo 3 TEST1 on the SD card, whose line 10 is POKE 65497,0: the machine does start at normal speed. Docs: docs/cpu-speed.md rewritten around the feature, README (feature bullet, Status, Performance, RAM), ROADMAP. DONE WHEN: the user confirms a program speeds up on hardware.

[2026-10-14 DONE] The user confirmed on hardware: "double speed works".

summary: Boot a 128 KB CoCo 3 to the BASIC prompt
description:
Stage 4 of the CoCo 3 plan. ONLY after the PIZERO-131 gate, and with PIZERO-135 decided.

DO: vendor tcc1014.[ch] (the GIME, 1612 lines at the pin) and font-gime.[ch] from upstream ~/github/xroar at the pinned a2d31903 into lib/xroar_core; update PROVENANCE.md and the library.json srcFilter; add a vo.h stub (its other deps: part, events, serialise, delegate are already vendored). Do NOT vendor coco3.c (1532 lines of desktop glue); write a CoCo 3 mode in lib/coco_machine instead: flat static 128 KB RAM, the GIME as the bus (tcc1014_mem_cycle, with the PIZERO-131 fast path), the existing PIAs, keyboard, DAC and FDC/disk path. 1.79 MHz is 8 instead of 16 ticks per access (tcc1014.c:832). A render_line sink takes every other of the GIME's 6-bit colour samples through a 64-entry RGB565 table from coco_pal_gime_to_rgb565() (coco_palette.h, matches upstream intensities) into the 320x240 framebuffer. In this mode the GIME owns palette, timer and interrupts; lib/coco_machine/src/gime_timer.h (which differs from upstream: zero reload, restart triggers, INIT0 gating, 910 vs 912 ticks per line) stays only for the CoCo 2 hybrid. coco3.rom (32 KB) loads from the card, with a boot page when missing (src/boot_messages.h style).

FIRST MILESTONE: 32 and 40 column text, 320 and 256 wide graphics. 640-wide modes are PIZERO-134. RAM: about 23 KB spare with the framebuffer kept.

DONE WHEN: on hardware coco3.rom boots to the CoCo 3 BASIC prompt, WIDTH 40 works, a palette POKE recolours, a GIME timer program runs, HSCREEN 320-wide modes draw; speed reported from [run].

DEPENDS ON: PIZERO-131 (gate), PIZERO-135.

Plan and reasoning: docs/coco3-plan.md; feasibility numbers: docs/coco3-feasibility.md (PIZERO-111).

[2026-09-28 note from PIZERO-164] Two-button joysticks: the CoCo 3 reads the second fire button of each stick on PIA0 PA2 (right) and PA3 (left) (upstream coco3.c:1361, joystick_read_buttons() & 15). In CoCo 3 mode, add a 'fire2' pad action that drives those bits; it must not exist in CoCo 2 mode, where PA2/PA3 are keyboard rows. [2026-10-13 STARTED on the user's word after PIZERO-131 closed. PIZERO-135's mode question is NOT decided; until it is, CoCo 3 mode will be its own firmware env, so nothing changes for the product build. STEP 1 DONE, ON THE HOST: tcc1014.[ch] and font-gime.[ch] vendored at the pinned a2d31903 (serialisation removed, as for the other parts; registered in part.c; library.json builds them; product build +6.5 KB flash, +8 bytes RAM). New lib/coco_machine/src/coco3_bus.h: 128 KB as two 64 KB halves (physical address modulo 128 KB, as upstream's RAM_ORG(17,9,0)), ROM/cart/RAM data movement after the GIME's decode, the video fetch, and a scanline sink that halves the 640 pixels around the active area into the 320x240 RGB565 framebuffer and centres the active lines (192 at row 24). New test/test_coco3_boot: the firmware's own 6809 core and PIAs with the GIME, wired as upstream's coco3.c, boot coco3.rom from COCO_ROM_DIR to the banner and OK in 3 emulated seconds; the frame dump showed the expected green screen with black text at the CoCo 2's position. NEXT: the firmware machine (coco_machine.cpp CoCo 3 mode: GIME as the bus, PIAs, keyboard, DAC, disk controller, the second 64 KB from the heap, video straight into g_fb) and a pizero_coco3 env.] [2026-10-13 DONE on hardware. Commit 276753f adds env pizero_coco3 (extends pizero_stream_60 with -DCOCO3; the product build is byte-identical). coco_machine.cpp, under #ifdef COCO3: coco3_init when the loaded ROM is 32 KB; RAM lo 64 KB from rp_mem_malloc, hi 64 KB from malloc; MC6809, two MC6821 (upstream coco3 defaults) and TCC1014-1987; coco_mem_cycle and coco_mem_nvma go through tcc1014_mem_cycle; coco3_cpu_cycle routes the PIAs (DAC on PIA1 writes), cartridge I/O (FDC, shared cart_io_write) and IL1; the GIME draws each scanline straight into g_fb (render_frame returns early, vdg_buffer shrinks to 4 bytes). main.cpp loads /coco/roms/coco3.rom (boot pages MSG_NOROM3_BODY / MSG_BADROM3_BODY). Static RAM 76.7%. HARDWARE (bench board C58D06257AE30E85, 8 GB card with coco3.rom added): the user saw it boot to OK and called it 'sluggish but not terrible'. [run] showed fps=29 cpu=~35000us per frame at 0.89 MHz, freezes=0; [aud] short=52% (sound at half rate). NOT DONE, filed as remainders: PIZERO-213 (the MMU fast path, needed even at 0.89 MHz), PIZERO-214 (check WIDTH 40, palette POKE, GIME timer, HSCREEN 320 on hardware), PIZERO-215 (CoCo 3 keyboard extras and fire2), PIZERO-216 (LOADM/BIN under a non-default MMU map), PIZERO-217 (tearing from drawing straight into g_fb; double-buffer envs unsupported). Already filed: PIZERO-134 (640-wide modes are halved), PIZERO-135 (mode selection: still a separate env), PIZERO-178 (render cost per mode).]

summary: 640-wide GIME modes and 80-column text
description:
Follow-on to PIZERO-133. The 640-wide GIME modes (including WIDTH 80 text) cannot use our 320x240 framebuffer: halving them makes 80-column text unreadable, and a 640x240 RGB565 buffer (307,200 bytes) does not fit. The route is per-scanline generation into libdvi's scanline queue (dvi_scanbuf_main_16bpp): two 1,280-byte line buffers instead of the framebuffer, which also frees 153,600 bytes. A real change to the scanout architecture, affecting the CoCo 2 path, the boot pages and the overlay too.

DONE WHEN: WIDTH 80 is readable on hardware and the CoCo 2 path still runs unchanged.

DEPENDS ON: PIZERO-133.

Plan and reasoning: docs/coco3-plan.md; feasibility numbers: docs/coco3-feasibility.md (PIZERO-111). SEEN ON HARDWARE 2026-10-19 (PIZERO-228): Sinistar's WIDTH 80 opening screen and the NitrOS-9 Level 2 boot message are unreadable on the board. The user describes it as characters copied to the screen wrong, with missing rows and gaps. Pixel dump of the screenshot: horizontal strokes come out as 2-on 2-off runs ('##..##') and vertical strokes survive only on some columns, so the halved text is worse than every-other-pixel decimation alone would suggest; port_render_scanline in lib/xroar_core/src/tcc1014/tcc1014.c (port_emit case 2) is where the 640-wide line is reduced. The full-width path here is the real fix; a cheaper interim (OR or average each pixel pair instead of dropping one) could make 80 columns legible meanwhile. STEP 1 2026-10-20, env pizero_coco3_640 (-DVIDEO_640 -DTCC1014_PORT_FULL): the framebuffer is 640x240 one-byte colours (153,600 bytes, the RGB565 buffer's size; RAM 79.1%, unchanged). The GIME port renderer emits all 640 pixels (tcc1014.c port_emit under TCC1014_PORT_FULL; TCC1014_PORT_W 640), coco3_bus.h stores them as 6-bit indices (coco3_pix_t), and core 1 scans out with libdvi dvi_static_framebuf_main_pal8, which looks each pair up in g_pal565[256] (0-63 GIME colours, 64-65 the card's ink and paper) and encodes on the SIO hardware TMDS encoder (tmds_encode_pal8_sio). Boot and overlay cards draw two bytes a pixel (coco_boot_card_present8); screenshots save 640x480 with each row twice (coco_boot_screenshot8). ON THE BOARD: the no-card page is steady and right, and WIDTH 80 text is readable (user). Telemetry at the prompt: fps 60, cpu 8.5-11.3 ms, under 0, skips 0. pizero_coco3 (halved), pizero_stream_60 and test_coco3_boot unchanged and passing. NEXT: the 214 check screens again, a full-screen animation at 1.79 MHz (the decode now writes twice the bytes), Sinistar's screen, then make it the pizero_coco3 default. CHECKS 2026-10-20 on pizero_coco3_640: the six pizero214.bas screens, screenshotted at 640x480 (SCR0010-0015), match the first run's 320x240 shots (SCR0001-0006) pixel for pixel at every other pixel and row, except 35 pixels on the timer screen, where the 0.89 MHz reading is 23.9 this time against 24 before (the count's start phase). Full-screen HCLS loop on HSCREEN 2 at 1.79 MHz: fps 60, cpu about 13.7 ms, late 0, slack about 2.2 ms. Screenshots are now 640x480 and about 308 KB, taking about 0.9 s against 0.2 s (the machine pauses meanwhile). CLOSED 2026-10-20: the user read WIDTH 80 text and Sinistar's 80-column opening screen on the board. VIDEO_640 and TCC1014_PORT_FULL are now in pizero_coco3 itself (pizero_coco3_640 folded in; RAM 79.1%; pizero_coco3_prof 81.7%), flashed. Docs: BUILD.md (env row, flag rows), pipeline.md, coco3-plan.md, coco3-feasibility.md, ROADMAP.md, README, coco3-titles.md. Left: slow 640x480 screenshots (PIZERO-237); the host test test_coco3_boot still builds the halved 320 path (no flags), so the 640 path has no host test yet (PIZERO-237 too). PIZERO-179's GIME half is done by this; its other chips stay there.

summary: CoCo 3: how the mode is chosen, and what audio does below real time
description:
Two decisions to settle with the user before PIZERO-133 is built.

1. MODE SELECTION: automatically when coco3.rom is on the card, by an autorun.txt directive, or a separate firmware build? Consider that a card may hold both CoCo 2 and CoCo 3 ROMs, and the F12 overlay (PIZERO-81) is a natural place for a choice later.

2. BELOW REAL TIME: if PIZERO-131 lands at about 80%, emulated time runs slow, so the DAC makes fewer samples than HDMI plays. The audio servo (lib/coco_machine/src/audio_servo.h) corrects only +/-0.13% by design, nowhere near 20%. Options: resample to fit (music plays about 20% low and slow, but continuous) or keep pitch and accept gaps.

COMPLETION: both answers recorded here with the reasoning, and reflected in docs/coco3-plan.md.

Plan and reasoning: docs/coco3-plan.md; feasibility numbers: docs/coco3-feasibility.md (PIZERO-111). DECIDED 2026-10-20 with the user: one firmware; machine = coco2 | coco3 in settings.txt (default coco2); a game's own NAME.TXT can say machine = coco3, and launching it switches automatically by restarting the board (the RAM layouts differ), with the choice carried across the restart. Audio below real time no longer arises: the CoCo 3 runs at full speed (PIZERO-213, 218, 220). STAGE 1 DONE: pizero_coco3 is now either machine. settings.h parses and writes machine; setup() reads settings.txt once before the ROMs to pick (g_coco3_mode, IS_COCO3()), loads coco3.rom or the CoCo 2 ROMs, falls back to a CoCo 2 with the ROM page shown 6 s when coco3.rom is missing or wrong, and passes the right ROM length to coco_machine_init. The CoCo 2's 24 KB vdg_buffer comes from the heap in COCO3 builds; a CoCo 2 draws into the 640-wide index framebuffer with coco_boot_blit_vdg_pizero8 (each pixel twice, palette in g_pal565[80..95]). On the board: CoCo 2 picture and sound right (user), fps 60, blit about 0.87 ms; machine = coco3 boots the CoCo 3 and RUN keeps it. Heap: 87,184 bytes before the machine (97,584 in the CoCo 3-only build: the CoCo 2 renderer's statics now link), 17,696 after the CoCo 3's 128 KB, so a bank-switched cartridge in CoCo 3 mode only fits up to about 1 KB + 16 KB. NEXT: per-game switching with a restart, and restart when settings.txt's machine changes. STAGE 2 DONE 2026-10-20: per-game switching. perform_launch asks machine_wanted(path) (settings.txt with the game's own file on top); if it differs and the card can start that machine (machine_available: coco3.rom 32 KB or bas12.rom 8 KB), switch_machine writes /coco/log/switch.txt ('coco3 what kind path'), shows 'STARTING THE COCO 3' and restarts with watchdog_reboot, tagging scratch[4] = MACHINE_SWITCH_MAGIC so the boot counts it as deliberate, not a freeze. setup() reads and deletes the file, believes it only after that tagged restart, boots that machine, skips autorun and launches the game (HO_LAUNCH). Saving settings.txt with a new machine restarts to the BASIC prompt (HO_BASIC); a game autorun starts that wants the other machine restarts into it with autorun as usual (HO_NORMAL). Three snags on the way, each seen on the board: (1) a RAM record (.uninitialized_data) did not survive: the boot reuses SRAM (as wd_post.cpp warns); (2) a core reset (AIRCR SYSRESETREQ) left the display's DMA and PIO running and the next boot stalled starting them, and the still-running watchdog restarted the board a second time; (3) the SDK's watchdog_reboot(0, ...) zeroes scratch[4], so the tag must be written after the call. (3) also broke PIZERO-51's USB_REPLUG_MAGIC tag, fixed the same way. The switch restart's chip_reset shows the RUN bit, so a handoff boot clears g_run_button_reset. ON THE BOARD (user): machine = coco2 saved from a CoCo 3 restarts as a CoCo 2; STARCAST.TXT with machine = coco3 launched from the CoCo 2's list restarts as a CoCo 3 and runs Starcast; a CoCo 2 game switches back; RUN returns to settings.txt's machine. PRODUCT: pizero_stream_60 now carries -DCOCO3 -DVIDEO_640 -DTCC1014_PORT_FULL (RAM 81.2%, below the CoCo 2-only 83.0% since the 24 KB VDG buffer moved to the heap); pizero_coco3 is an alias of it. Every firmware env builds; 261 host tests pass. Cost to the CoCo 2: free heap with the machine running 59,232 bytes against 74,152 in the CoCo 2-only build (32 KB bank-switched carts still fit); its picture blit is faster on the 640-wide path (0.87 against 1.56 ms). CoCo 3 headroom about 17 KB. Docs: README, SETTINGS.md (machine), BUILD.md, coco3-plan.md (questions answered), coco3-feasibility.md, pipeline.md, ROADMAP.md.

summary: BIN and CART files in the F12 overlay list
description:
Remainder of PIZERO-81a, which shipped the overlay catalogue with .dsk images only. PIZERO-81 always meant all three entry types the port can boot (autorun.txt @DISK, @DIRECT .bin, @CART .rom/.ccc). A BIN or CART entry cannot go in a drive, so it only makes sense together with a way to START an entry (PIZERO-81d) and the ENTER decision (PIZERO-115).

DO: extend src/dsk_catalog.h (rules and host tests in test/test_dsk_catalog) with an entry type, scanning /coco/bin and /coco/roms as coco_boot_resolve does; show the type in the list; drive keys 0-3 apply to DSK only.

DEPENDS ON: PIZERO-81d, PIZERO-115.

[2026-09-27 BUILT with PIZERO-81d: src/dsk_catalog.h now lists one kind at a time (enum cat_kind: CAT_DSK, CAT_BIN, CAT_CART) from the kind's folder (/coco/dsk, /coco/bin, /coco/roms) then /coco. CART takes .rom and .ccc but not the machine's own ROMs (bas*, extbas*, coco3*); disk11.rom is kept since it is the Disk BASIC cartridge. Left/Right in the overlay switch list and rescan, so only one 8 KB list is ever in RAM. Titles < DISKS > / < PROGRAMS > / < CARTRIDGES >, a legend per list, and an empty-list message saying which folder to use; all checked by host tests.]

[2026-09-27 Per the user, cartridge files are .ccc: the CART list now takes .ccc only (from /coco/roms then /coco), leaving .rom to the machine's own ROMs, so the bas*/extbas*/coco3* exclusion is gone and disk11.rom is no longer listed (the DISKS list's ENTER still installs it).]

The overlay now loads the exact file chosen (coco_boot_load_cart_path) instead of resolving a name, and coco_boot_load_cart_named (autorun.txt @CART, and disk11.rom) searches /coco/cart, then /coco/roms, then /coco, with .CCC appended to a bare name in /coco/cart. AUTORUN.md says so.]

summary: Cartridges of 2, 4, 8 and 16 KB, not just 8 KB
description:
User request 2026-09-27. The machine kept an 8 KB cartridge buffer and hardwired an 8 KB mirror (lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp, the S=3 read: cart_rom[A & 0x1FFF]), and every loader required exactly 8192 bytes, so a 16 KB .ccc was refused (the F12 overlay said '16K CARTS NOT YET SUPPORTED').

HARDWARE: the cartridge window is $C000-$FEFF, just under 16 KB. Cartridges came in 2, 4, 8 and 16 KB; smaller ones repeat through the window because they do not decode the upper address lines. XRoar handles this with a size mask.

DO: coco_machine_install_cart_sized(rom, len) with a power-of-two mask (install_cart keeps meaning 8 KB); the cartridge buffer becomes 16 KB where RAM allows; loaders report the size read; the overlay and autorun.txt @CART accept 2/4/8/16 KB. The double-buffered fallback env 'pizero' is at 99.5% static RAM and cannot take +8 KB, so it keeps an 8 KB limit and says so.

NOT IN SCOPE: bank-switched cartridges larger than 16 KB, which need per-cartridge mappers.

DONE WHEN: a 16 KB .ccc starts from the F12 overlay on hardware, and an 8 KB one still does.

[2026-09-27 BUILT, not yet on hardware. coco_machine.cpp: cart_mask (size - 1) replaces the hardwired 0x1FFF in the S=3 read, set by the new coco_machine_install_cart_sized(rom, len); install_cart keeps meaning 8 KB. src/dsk_catalog.h cat_cart_size_ok(size, max) holds the rule (2/4/8/16 KB, no bigger than the buffer; host test). coco_boot_load_cart_path/_named take (buf, max, &len), check the size with f_stat BEFORE touching the buffer so a refused file leaves the installed cart intact, and serve the overlay, autorun.txt @CART and disk11.rom alike. main.cpp COCO_CART_MAX is 16384 under HDMI_DATA_ISLAND (the product build, RAM 73.2% to 74.7%) and 8192 otherwise, where the overlay says '16K CARTS NOT IN THIS BUILD'. 116 host tests pass.]

[2026-09-27 DONE: confirmed on hardware by the user ("the 16k cartridge works"). A serial capture of the same session shows every size loading and starting from the F12 overlay: Popcorn 2 KB; Galactic Attack, Quasar Commander, Space Assault 4 KB; Color Robot Battle, Mega-Bug 8 KB; Fahrfall (Pandemic Edition) and Tetris 16 KB. Long names with spaces and brackets load fine. Bank-switched carts over 16 KB (Mind Roll 32 KB and Dunjunz 64 KB on CoCo 1/2; XRoar's GMC type) and the CoCo 3-only unbanked 32 KB titles remain out of scope.]

summary: GM0-GM6 graphics modes render too slowly: Popcorn runs at 50 fps, Space Assault at 59
description:
Found 2026-09-27 in a serial capture while testing cartridges from the F12 overlay (PIZERO-139). Two titles push the frame over budget in the render phase alone:

  Popcorn (2 KB cart)        [vdg] mode=gm5  render ~7,500 us  fps=50 (one second at 49)
  Space Assault (4 KB cart)  [vdg] mode=gm4  render ~3,750 us  fps=59

for comparison, alpha/SG4 renders in ~450 us and RG6 is LUT-driven. With cpu ~11,100-11,500 us and blit ~1,600 us, Popcorn's frame is ~20.2 ms against 16.67 ms, so pacing resyncs, emulated time runs at ~83% and the audio producer falls short with it (the PIZERO-119 failure class).

CAUSE: lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp render_graphics_frame (GM 0-6, AMOLED-60) expands every pixel with per-bit / per-cell loops and an inner hrep loop into rowbuf, then packs nibbles. PIZERO-119 only fixed its row repeats (pack once, memcpy) and LUT'd SG4; RG6 has its own LUT path (render_rg6_frame).

FIX DIRECTION: the same move PIZERO-119 made: per-byte lookup tables that emit the packed 4bpp nibbles directly. RG modes: one table per (fg,bg) set indexed by the data byte (rebuilt only when CSS changes); CG modes: 2-bit cells through a small table. Handle hrep 1/2/4 by table width. Verify byte-identical output against the current renderer on the host first (.ref/lutcheck.cpp and sg4check.cpp are the precedent), then measure render= on hardware with Popcorn (gm5) and Space Assault (gm4).

DONE WHEN: every GM 0-6 mode renders well under 1 ms on hardware and Popcorn holds 60 fps with the audio shortfall at 0%.

[2026-09-27 BUILT, not yet measured on hardware. lib/coco_machine/src/vdg_pack.h: vdg_gm_expand() is the old per-pixel rule verbatim; vdg_gm_lut_build() turns it into a 256-entry table of packed output bytes per data byte (8 for the 16-byte-row modes, 4 for the 32-byte-row modes), rebuilt only when gm or css changes; vdg_render_gm() does one lookup and memcpy per data byte and memcpy for the row repeats. render_graphics_frame in coco_machine.cpp now just calls it (GM_nLPR moved to VDG_GM_NLPR; static_assert added for PAL_BLACK and PAL_DARK_GREEN). HOST TESTS: whole frames for GM 0-6, both colour sets, six base addresses, plus every byte value in every mode, byte-identical to a verbatim copy of the old renderer. Checked the tests bite: a planted CG shift bug fails both; a planted nibble swap does not, correctly, because every GM 0-6 pixel is at least doubled horizontally so both nibbles of a packed byte are always equal. RAM 75.1% (+1.7 KB, the table). CHECK ON HARDWARE: render= for Popcorn (gm5) and Space Assault (gm4), fps 60, [aud] short 0%.]

[2026-09-27 SECOND DEFECT, reported by the user on the table-driven build: Popcorn showed only half a screen of game; its pixels should be double height. Pre-existing, since the host tests prove the new renderer matches the old one exactly. CAUSE: on a CoCo the SAM, not the VDG, generates video addresses, so the SAM's V mode sets the bytes between data rows and the display lines per row; the renderer took both from the VDG mode alone. Popcorn pairs VDG GM5 (one line per row) with a SAM mode that doubles rows, so 96 data rows were drawn once each in the top half. FIX: the SAM V register ($FFC0-$FFC5) is now shadowed as g_m.sam_v (reset by the cold reset), vdg_gfx_geometry(gm, sam_v) in vdg_pack.h gives the row stride and repeat from the SAM when it is in a graphics mode (1-6) and falls back to the VDG mode's own otherwise, and both render_graphics_frame and render_rg6_frame use it (so RG6 under SAM V4 doubles too). The VDG mode still decides how a byte becomes pixels. The [vdg] telemetry line now also prints sam=V. Host tests: SAM geometry table, SAM agreeing with VDG reproduces the old frames exactly, and GM5 under SAM V3 matches GM3 over the whole screen. 120 tests pass.]

[2026-09-27 DONE: confirmed on hardware by the user ("that looks good"): Popcorn now fills the screen. The serial capture shows Popcorn's game screen is VDG gm7c with SAM V4 (256x96, rows doubled), holding 60 fps for all 61 s with render at most 237 us and no audio shortfall. The GM 0-6 table renderer is proven byte-identical to the old one by host tests; its hardware timing in GM4/GM5 was not captured in this session and is filed as PIZERO-141 rather than holding this open.]

GM5 was not seen in this session (Popcorn's game screen is gm7c/SAM V4, already measured at 237 us max), but GM4 and GM5 share the same table renderer and the host tests cover all GM 0-6 modes.]

summary: Bank-switched cartridges over 16 KB (Games Master Cartridge banking)
description:
User request 2026-09-27, after PIZERO-139 made 2-16 KB carts work. The cartridge window is 16 KB, so bigger carts switch 16 KB banks. XRoar treats any image over 16 KB as a Games Master Cartridge (~/github/xroar/src/gmc.c, cart.c:360-375): reads of $C000-$FEFF come from rom[bank | (A & 0x3FFF)]; a write to an EVEN address in $FF40-$FF5F sets bank = (D << 14) & ((size - 1) & 0x3C000); an ODD address goes to its SN76489 sound chip; reset selects bank 0. Titles in XRoar's list that run on a CoCo 1/2: Mind Roll (32 KB, 1988 Tandy) and Dunjunz (64 KB, 2020). Predator (64 KB) and RoboCop (128 KB) are CoCo 3 only.

MEMORY: a permanent 64 KB buffer would take the RAM the 128 KB CoCo 3 plan (PIZERO-133) needs, so a banked image is allocated on the heap only while it is installed, and freed when another cartridge replaces it; a launch that will not fit says so and leaves the running program alone.

DO: bank switching in lib/coco_machine (switching moves the cart pointer, so reads cost nothing extra); $FF40-$FF5F writes go to the bank register instead of the FDC while a banked cart is in; overlay and autorun.txt @CART accept power-of-two images of 32 KB and up that fit in memory.

NOT IN THIS ISSUE: the SN76489 sound chip (odd-address writes are counted but silent), filed separately.

DONE WHEN: a 32 KB and a 64 KB banked cart start from the F12 overlay on hardware, and plain carts and disks still work after switching back.

[2026-09-27 BUILT, not yet on hardware. lib/coco_machine/src/cart_gmc.h holds the rules (cart_is_banked_size: power of two 32-256 KB; gmc_bank_offset; even/odd register), 3 host tests including every D for every size staying inside the image. coco_machine: coco_machine_install_cart_banked(rom, len) starts in bank 0; an even $FF40-$FF5F write moves cart_rom to the selected bank inside cart_base (reads cost nothing extra); odd writes (SN76489) are counted in csg_writes; FDC reads return $FF while a banked cart is in; cold reset returns to bank 0. main.cpp install_cart_file() installs any cart file: plain ones in the fixed 16 KB buffer, banked ones in a heap buffer of their own size, released when another cart replaces it (unplugged first, so nothing reads freed memory). The overlay pre-check refuses a banked cart that will not fit with 'NOT ENOUGH MEMORY FOR nK'. disk11.rom and autorun.txt @CART go through the same path (coco_boot_resolve_cart), so @CART can name a banked cart too; the old coco_boot_load_cart_named is gone. Boot prints '[mem] free heap N bytes'. 123 host tests pass; product RAM 75.1% static.
ALSO FIXED: PIZERO-140's 2 KB renderer table had pushed the double-buffered fallback envs (pizero, pizero_60hz) over RAM, so they failed to link. dsk_catalog.h now gives those builds a 64-entry list (128 in the product build), and pizero, pizero_60hz, pizero_stream and pizero_stream_60 all build (99.1%, 99.1%, 75.0%, 75.1%).]

[2026-09-27 When testing a banked cart on hardware, also listen: PIZERO-143's SN76489 is confirmed working via POKE, and a GMC title that uses it shows [csg] writes on serial. Note two boards are in use; name the board (USB serial) with each flash.]

[2026-09-28 The user is not sure they have a bank-switched cartridge image to test with. Candidates that run on a CoCo 1/2: Mind Roll (1988, 32 KB) and Dunjunz (2020, 64 KB, GMC; its author distributes it). Until one is found this stays open; the code path is host-tested (cart_gmc.h).]

[2026-10-15 CLOSED at about 80%, the user's call] The banked-cartridge code is built and host-tested (cart_gmc.h) and all product envs build, but it has never run a real bank-switched image on the board, since no image is to hand. The user will let someone else test it later; that test is PIZERO-226.

summary: SN76489 sound chip for Games Master Cartridge titles
description:
Remainder of PIZERO-142. The Games Master Cartridge carries an SN76489 sound chip, written at ODD addresses in $FF40-$FF5F. PIZERO-142 counts those writes (coco_machine_cart_csg_writes) but produces no sound, so a GMC title that uses it (modern homebrew such as Dunjunz is the likely case; Mind Roll predates the GMC) runs silent or partly silent.

DO: port ~/github/xroar/src/sn76489.c (XRoar configures it at 4 MHz, gmc.c sn76489_configure) and mix its output into the DAC audio path the ring buffer feeds (lib/coco_machine audio_integrate / the 48 kHz producer), without breaking the PIZERO-121 rate servo or the CPU budget. First check a title actually writes it: the csg_writes counter shows that without any sound code.

DONE WHEN: a GMC title's music plays on hardware and ordinary DAC sound is unchanged.

[2026-09-27 STARTED at the user's request. Approach: a fresh integer implementation in a host-tested header rather than vendoring XRoar's float sn76489.c (which pulls filter.h, part, serialise), matching the behaviour XRoar models: 3 square tones at 4 MHz / (32 N), N 10-bit with 0 = 1024; a 15-bit noise LFSR reset to $4000 on each noise write, white = parity of bits 0-1, periodic = bit 0, clocked at one of three rates or by tone 3; 4-bit attenuation in 2 dB steps, 15 = off; unipolar outputs summed. Stepped per 48 kHz output sample on core 0 in the same loop as the CPU, so writes land between samples where the program made them. Authentic placement first (only with a GMC cart in). OPEN QUESTION for the user: also expose it with Disk BASIC in, at an address the disk controller does not use, as our own extension.]

[2026-09-27 BUILT, not yet heard on hardware. lib/coco_machine/src/csg_sn76489.h: integer model of XRoar's behaviour (250 kHz chip tick; tones 125 kHz / N with 0 = 1024; 15-bit LFSR reset to $4000 per noise write, white = parity bits 0-1, periodic = bit 0, reload 16/32/64 or tone 3; SN_LEVEL 2 dB steps with full scale a quarter of the DAC swing per channel; latch/data protocol incl. a data byte replacing a volume; writes inside 32 chip clocks (SN_READY_TICKS 115 event ticks) ignored, as XRoar does). Starts silent rather than mimicking the chip's half-random power-on state. 9 host tests: silence, divider bytes, volume, 1 kHz pitch at N=125, a 125 kHz tone averaging to half level (no aliasing), the 15-step periodic pulse, white noise and its reset, tone-3 noise clocking, the ready gap. coco_machine.cpp: odd $FF40-$FF5F writes with a banked cart go to sn_write (dropped if too soon); audio_integrate adds sn_render(tk) to each sample, averaging the chip over that sample's event ticks; the chip is reset and idle on any cart change and on cold reset, and costs nothing until first written. Serial prints '[csg] writes=N dropped=M' once a second while a program uses it. RAM 75.3%; all four envs build; 132 host tests pass.
STILL OPEN: the user's question whether to expose it with Disk BASIC in, at an address the disk controller does not use, as our own extension.]

[2026-09-27 DECIDED by the user: available all the time, not only with a GMC; a settings page (PIZERO-53) will switch features like this on and off. IMPLEMENTED: without a banked cart, the odd mirrors of the disk controller's drive latch ($FF41/43/45/47 and $FF51-57, cart_gmc.h csg_on_latch_mirror, host-tested) go to the chip; the latch at $FF40 and the WD279x at $FF48-$FF4B are untouched, since Disk BASIC and OS-9 write the latch only at $FF40. That puts the chip at $FF41, where GMC software writes it, with Disk BASIC still in. Trade-off: a real FD-502 would take $FF41 as the latch; coco_machine_csg_always(false) restores that, for the settings page. With a GMC in, the authentic routing applies (every odd address). README documents $FF41. All four envs build; 133 host tests pass.]

[2026-09-27 DONE: heard on hardware by the user ("yeah it's playing"), with no GMC plugged in, on board 1D21CC1CBE17D6F6 at the Disk BASIC prompt. Typed over serial: POKE &HFF41,142 / 15 / 144 (tone 1, N = 254, ~492 Hz, full volume): [csg] writes 1-3 with none dropped, [aud] tone ~1,780/s; POKE &HFF41,159 silenced it (tone 0/s). Also reproduced on board C58D06257AE30E85. Hearing a GMC title's own music depends on a banked cart and is folded into PIZERO-142's hardware test. The Disk BASIC prompt, SOUND, disks and the audio servo were unaffected throughout (prod 48,00x/s, no underruns).]

summary: See the other four boot pages on a real screen

Remainder of PIZERO-92, which closed when the NO SD CARD page was seen on a TV (2026-09-27). The other pages are written and host-tested but not yet seen on hardware:

summary: Settings in /coco/settings.txt, each a runtime switch
description:
User direction 2026-09-27: collect the firmware's switches into settings that can be toggled at runtime and are stored on the SD card. There is to be NO settings GUI: the file is edited as text (PIZERO-146), so the file is the source of truth.

SETTINGS (proposed to the user, no objections):
  sn76489            on|off            SN76489 at $FF41 without a GMC (PIZERO-143; coco_machine_csg_always)
  volume             0-15              overall level (today AUDIO_DAC_GAIN 60, fixed at build)
  artifact_colours   off|blue-red|red-blue   PMODE 4 artifact colour or plain mono (today always on, phase fixed by ARTIFACT_PHASE_LEGACY)
  gime_palette       on|off            CoCo 3-style palette at $FFB0 (today build flag GIME_PALETTE)
  gime_timer         on|off            CoCo 3-style timer at $FF90 (today build flag GIME_TIMER)
  run_skips_autorun  on|off            RUN goes straight to BASIC (PIZERO-116)
  serial_keyboard    on|off            typing into the CoCo over USB serial

FORMAT: /coco/settings.txt, one 'name = value' per line, '#' comments, case-insensitive, the same plain style as autorun.txt. A missing file or line means the default; an unknown name or bad value is reported on serial and ignored, never fatal.

DESIGN: one table of settings with get/set/apply, each applying immediately, so the editor (PIZERO-146) only has to re-read the file after saving. The parser is pure and host-tested, like dsk_catalog.h.

NOT HERE: writing the file (PIZERO-146), a SAM double-speed cap (needs PIZERO-132/48 first).

DONE WHEN: each setting, changed in the file on a PC and booted, visibly or audibly takes effect on hardware, and a malformed file boots with defaults and a serial report.

[2026-09-27 ADDED at the user's request: a default colour palette.
  palette = NAME|factory   loads /coco/pal/NAME.pal as the power-on palette; 'factory' or no line keeps g_pal_factory (coco_machine.cpp)
This is the user-global layer PIZERO-55 planned between per-title palettes and the factory default (fallback order per-title <name>.pal -> user default -> factory). .pal FORMAT, shared with PIZERO-55's per-title files and editable in the PIZERO-146 editor: plain text, 'N = #RRGGBB' per line for palette index N (0 green, 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, 4 white, 5 cyan, 6 magenta, 7 orange, 8 black, 9 dark green, ...), '#' comments; entries not listed keep their factory colour; colours round to RGB565. Applies through coco_machine_palette_set and becomes what coco_machine_palette_reset (and the cold reset) restores. Parser host-tested with the settings parser.]

[2026-09-27 RENAMED sound_chip to sn76489 at the user's request ('too generic'): settings for sound hardware are named after the chip, leaving room for others (e.g. orchestra90).]

[2026-09-27 BUILT, not yet on hardware. src/settings.h: struct coco_settings, settings_defaults, settings_parse_line (case-insensitive, '#' comments on their own line or after a value, reports SET_UNKNOWN / SET_BAD_VALUE / SET_SYNTAX), pal_parse_line ('N = #RRGGBB'), settings_rgb565 (rounded); 6 host tests. artifact_colours takes on|off|swapped (not blue-red/red-blue: 'swapped' is unambiguous relative to today's phase; artifact_colors also accepted). coco_boot.cpp: coco_boot_load_settings() and coco_boot_load_palette() read the files with f_gets, reporting each bad line with its number. coco_machine: runtime switches coco_machine_set_volume (gain = AUDIO_DAC_GAIN * v / 10, the SN76489 scaled with it), set_artifact (replaces the ARTIFACT_PHASE_LEGACY build choice, which now only sets the default), set_gime_palette / set_gime_timer (runtime gates inside the existing build flags; off removes the registers from the bus and resets palette or timer), palette_set_default (g_pal_default, which palette_reset and the cold reset restore). main.cpp: settings_defaults at the top of setup, load + settings_apply right after coco_machine_init and before AUTORUN, a '[settings] ...' line listing every value; run_skips_autorun gates the PIZERO-116 skip; serial_keyboard gates next_keychar. SETTINGS.md documents it all with an example, linked from README. All four envs build, no new warnings; 139 host tests pass.]

[2026-09-27 REVISED at the user's direction, superseding the palette parts above: NO palette files or named styles for now (they would need palette editors to be any good). Instead one setting per 6847 color overrides it directly in settings.txt: color_green, color_yellow, color_blue, color_red, color_white, color_cyan, color_magenta, color_orange, color_black, color_dark_green, color_dark_orange, color_bright_orange = #RRGGBB; colors without a line keep the default. The 'palette = NAME' setting, /coco/pal/*.pal and coco_boot_load_palette are gone. ALSO at the user's direction: American spellings only, and only one form accepted: artifact_colors (artifact_colours is now rejected as unknown), color_ (colour_ rejected). coco_settings carries color[16] + color_set; settings_apply passes them to coco_machine_palette_set_default. SETTINGS.md rewritten to match. All four envs build; 138 host tests pass.]

[2026-09-27 DONE at ~80%: the file loads at boot and re-applies on save (PIZERO-146), and on hardware sn76489 and gime_palette changed from the file took effect at once. Seeing each remaining setting's effect is filed as PIZERO-151.]

summary: On-screen text editor for /coco/settings.txt
description:
User direction 2026-09-27: no settings GUI. Settings are changed by editing /coco/settings.txt directly, in a plain text editor on the CoCo Zero's own screen, opened from the F12 overlay. On save the file is written back to the SD card and the settings are re-read and applied (PIZERO-145), so a change takes effect without a reboot.

summary: Orchestra-90CC: two 8-bit stereo DACs at $FF7A/$FF7B
description:
User request 2026-09-27, from a survey of sound add-ons. Tandy's Orchestra-90CC (1985) is two 8-bit DACs, left at $FF7A and right at $FF7B; music software pushes samples through them. XRoar's whole model is ~/github/xroar/src/orch90.c (158 lines): the write handler stores the byte and sets the external left/right level (D / 255). Its own music program ships in the cartridge ROM (XRoar loads 'orch90').

DO: decode $FF7A/$FF7B writes (no conflict with the disk controller at $FF40-$FF5F, so it can be always available like the SN76489, PIZERO-143), hold the two levels, and mix them into the audio samples through the same integrate-and-average as the DAC. Setting: orchestra90 = on|off in /coco/settings.txt (PIZERO-145).

THE ONE REAL DECISION: STEREO. The HDMI path sends the same sample to both channels today (main.cpp stream_audio fill: lr[2f] = lr[2f+1]). Honouring left/right means carrying two channels through the ring (coco_machine_audio_read) and the data-island encoder; decide whether to do that here or mix to mono first and file stereo separately.

DONE WHEN: an Orchestra-90 program plays on hardware.

[2026-10-22 BUILT, awaiting the user's ears.] The stereo decision was already made by PIZERO-250 (stereo ring and data islands), so the Orchestra-90 is stereo from the start.
- lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp: orch_owns/orch_write decode writes to $FF7A (left) and $FF7B (right) in the CoCo 2 write path and in coco3_cpu_cycle ahead of the GIME decode (free addresses on both machines). Not through the multiplexer (PIZERO-253): the card has its own jacks, as XRoar's non-muxed external audio. Full scale 4,700 mV (XRoar's D/255 of the whole line), scaled by volume (orch_levels, recomputed on a volume change).
- Exact timing: lib/coco_machine/src/audio_integ.h gains a second level (acc2; audio_integ_step2, audio_integ_run2): the left DAC rides with the line, the right as its difference, so each sample is the exact average of each DAC. test_audio_integ: test_two_levels_match_one_each (each level equals a one-level integrator of it alone, sample for sample) and test_run2_spans_match_steps; both mutation-checked.
- Setting orchestra90 = on | off (src/settings.h; on for cocozero, off for the stock coco2/coco3, where a cartridge's own file can turn it on). Telemetry [orch] writes=N. coco_machine_set_orchestra90 / coco_machine_orch_writes.
- docs/ay-checks/orch90.bas, saved as ORCH90 on AYTEST.DSK: a BASIC buzz left then right, then a machine-code loop at $7000 writing both DACs (sawtooths about 500 Hz left and 830 Hz right) about 42,000 times a second. On the board: 133,472 writes (exactly the program's), frame 8.9 ms during the loop (6.8 at rest), no late frames, no underruns.
- Docs: docs/sound.md (an Orchestra-90CC section, the At a glance row, the loudness table, the test program list, the multiplexer section and diagram), SETTINGS.md, README, ROADMAP.
Host tests 286 (6 skipped) pass; RAM 85.1 percent product (stream 84.9, wavmeas 81.7, coco3 85.2).
Still to do for DONE: the user hears ORCH90 (left, right, then both sides); the Orchestra-90's own music program needs its ROM on the card.

[2026-10-23 DONE, closed at the user's word: ORCH90 (docs/ay-checks/orch90.bas) heard on hardware, its machine-code stereo loop at 42,000 writes a second per DAC. Running the Orchestra-90's own music program, which needs its cartridge ROM on the card, is filed as PIZERO-260.]

summary: AY-3-8910 / YM2149 sound chip
description:
User request 2026-09-27, from a survey of sound add-ons. General Instrument's AY-3-8910 (and the compatible Yamaha YM2149): 3 square tones and noise like the SN76489, plus a hardware envelope generator and per-channel tone/noise mixing; the ZX Spectrum 128 / Amstrad CPC / MSX sound. XRoar added a model in 2024 (~/github/xroar/src/ay891x.c, 587 lines, from the data sheet and the reverse-engineered die in github.com/lvd2/ay-3-8910_reverse_engineered).

ON THE COCO it appeared in homebrew add-ons such as the CoCo PSG cartridge (a YM2149). BEFORE BUILDING: confirm the addresses real CoCo AY/YM hardware uses and name software that targets it, so the port has something to be tested against.

DO: a fresh integer model in a host-tested header, as PIZERO-143 did for the SN76489, mixed into the audio samples the same way. Setting named after the chip (e.g. ay8910 = on|off, PIZERO-145).

DONE WHEN: a program written for CoCo AY/YM hardware plays on hardware. [2026-10-22 SURVEY (user: 'do the survey first'). CoCo AY/YM hardware found:
(1) CoCo PSG (zippster278, modern homebrew cartridge, YM2149 at 1 or 2 MHz, plus 512K flash, 512K SRAM, two joystick ports): YM2149 register select $FF5E (write, 4 bits), data $FF5F (read/write), control $FF5D (bit 0 clock: 0 = 2 MHz, 1 = 1 MHz; bits 1-5 gameport selects, flash/SRAM write enable, autostart, flash programming), bank registers $FF5A/$FF5B. Source: MAME src/devices/bus/coco/coco_psg.cpp (SCS offsets 0x1A-0x1F) and the CoCo PSG user's manual. Software: the CoCo Chiptunes Player (zippster278; plays YM/OPL music converted to .CCT; needs a CoCo SDC and a 6309, so not runnable here), and Sierra's CoCo 3 OS-9 games patched for the PSG (Color Computer Archive, 2026-08-22, 'Disks/Games/Sierra Games (SSC)/': King's Quest I-IV, Space Quest 1-2, Police Quest, Leisure Suit Larry, Manhunter 1-2, Gold Rush, Black Cauldron, Mother Goose; these are Sierra's 512K CoCo 3 titles, so they wait on PSRAM, PIZERO-244).
(2) Tandy Speech/Sound Cartridge 26-3144A: an AY-3-8913 and SP0256-AL2 behind a PIC 7040 microcontroller; the CoCo writes commands to $FF7E (status read there) and resets via $FF7D, so emulating it means emulating the PIC's command protocol, not a bare AY. Same Sierra patches support it.
(3) Speech Systems Symphony-12 (and the Philharmonic-12 reproduction kit, go4retro): four AY-3-8910s through a PIA, 12 voices; address map not found (MAME coco_sym12.cpp was unreachable). Software: Lyra 1.2 with a Symphony 12 enhancer (archive, 2026-01-20), the Sierra patches.
(4) Tandy Deluxe Color Computer (cancelled 1984 prototype, three boards known): AY-3-8913 at $FF38 data, $FF39 address latch; upstream XRoar models it (src/dragon/deluxecoco.c, with src/ay891x.c). Almost no software.
Also: CocoSOUND (RETRO Innovations, dual AY/YM, not yet sold). Upstream XRoar emulates none of the cartridges; MAME emulates CoCo PSG, SSC and Symphony-12.
RECOMMENDATION: emulate the CoCo PSG's YM2149 at $FF5E/$FF5F with the $FF5D clock bit (default 1 MHz as MAME), skipping its flash, SRAM and joystick ports; it has the modern software and a reference emulation. No existing PSG software runs on this board today (player needs SDC + 6309, Sierra needs 512K), so 'done' becomes: our own test program (register writes for tones, noise, the envelope) plays on hardware and the model matches upstream XRoar's ay891x.c in a host test; the Sierra games are the real-software test once PSRAM gives a 512K CoCo 3.] [2026-10-22 DONE, confirmed on hardware by the user. Built as one bank of four AY chips with three address front-ends (user: 'is it feasible to instantiate a AY for each cartridge and map them accordingly to the same chip(s)?'): lib/coco_machine/src/psg_ay8910.h, pure integer, from the data sheet with XRoar's ay891x.c and MAME's ay8910.cpp as references (difference from XRoar, deliberate: a channel with tone and noise both off is steadily on, as on the chip, so sample playback works). Front-ends: CoCo PSG $FF5D-$FF5F (chip 0, 2 or 1 MHz), Symphony-12 PIA $FF60-$FF63 (chips 0-3, 14.31818/16 MHz, from MAME coco_sym12.cpp), Deluxe CoCo $FF38/$FF39 (chip 0, 14.31818/8 MHz as XRoar). Wired in coco_machine.cpp for both machines (CoCo 2 read and write paths, coco3_cpu_cycle ahead of the GIME decode), rendered in audio_sample like the SN76489, reset with the machine. Settings coco_psg and symphony12 (profile: on in cocozero, off in coco2/coco3) and deluxe_psg (off everywhere: on a CoCo 2 $FF38/$FF39 mirror PIA1). Telemetry [ay] writes=N chips=bitmask. Host tests: test/test_psg_ay8910 (15: pitch, masks, levels and mixer, noise period 2^17-1, all ten envelope shapes, envelope rate, render timing, each front-end, mix scaling and silent-chip skip), test_settings profile checks. RAM 81.8% (pizero_stream 81.2%, pizero_wavmeas 78.0%). Hardware (cocozero): docs/ay-checks/psg.bas (chord, envelope, noise: 'yes all that', [ay] writes=23 chips=1) and docs/ay-checks/sym12.bas (four chips build a C major chord); both saved on the card in AYTEST.DSK. First four-chip run overran (16.0 ms a frame, 58 fps, ring empty, 'a little distorted'): a 64-bit division per chip per sample; fixed with 32-bit timing and by skipping chips whose three levels are 0. After: 6.5 ms idle, 8.3 ms one chip, 12.9 ms four, 0 late, 0 underruns, 'better now'. Not done, filed: PIZERO-248 (render cost, CoCo 3 at 1.79 MHz), PIZERO-249 (Speech/Sound Cartridge), PIZERO-250 (Symphony-12 stereo), PIZERO-251 (real software: Lyra 1.2, the Sierra PSG games). The Deluxe front-end is host-tested only.]

summary: autorun.txt: @DISK alone runs the disk's program, and a missing name is reported
description:
Found testing PIZERO-147 on hardware (2026-09-27): the user wrote '@DISK SPACEWARP.DSK' (saved as 'space-warp.dsk' and 'spacewrp.DSK' on the way) and expected Spacewarp to start. Two gaps, both silent:
1. A name autorun.txt gives that is not on the card was skipped with no message at all; for @DISK no disk was mounted, and nothing on screen said why.
2. @DISK only mounts the disk. Running something needs a typed line after it, whereas the F12 overlay's ENTER on a disk runs its first program; the two paths disagreed.

DECIDED with the user: (a) when autorun.txt names a disk and has NO typed lines, run the disk's first program the way the overlay does (RSDOS directory via rsdos_dir.h, RUN"X" or LOADM"X":EXEC after the autorun warmup). With typed lines present they are typed exactly as before, so existing files behave the same; the default disk (no @DISK) never auto-runs. (b) a name in @DISK, @CART or @DIRECT that is not found shows a boot page naming it and logs it on serial, then boot carries on without it.

DONE WHEN: on hardware, '@DISK SPACEWARP.DSK' alone starts Spacewarp at power-on, and a misspelt name shows the page.

[2026-09-27 BUILT, not yet on hardware. main.cpp boot: each directive's name is resolved on its own; a miss logs '[autorun] @X NAME: not found on the card, skipped' and the first miss shows a boot page (boot_messages.h MSG_ARMISS_*, host-tested with a 63-character name) for 3 s. A missing @CART now falls back to disk11.rom (before, the whole Disk BASIC setup was skipped and the machine came up in plain Color BASIC with no disk); a missing @DISK falls back to the default disk; a missing @DIRECT boots normally. When @DISK named a disk that mounted and there are no typed lines, disk_run_command (the overlay's RSDOS path) queues RUN"X" or LOADM"X":EXEC with the 180-frame warmup; the default disk never auto-runs. AUTORUN.md documents both. 153 host tests pass.]

[2026-09-27 The user saw the page flash by and asked for a key to dismiss it. boot_wait(max_ms) in main.cpp holds a boot page until a key or the timeout, servicing USBHost.task() itself (loop() has not started) and counting a serial byte as a key. The not-found page now waits up to 30 s ('PRESS ANY KEY' added to its detail; still within the tested 3 rows); AUTORUN SKIPPED (2.5 s) and COLOR BASIC ONLY (4 s) keep their timeouts but a key skips them. Before the machine runs, hid_keyboard_apply only records presses (g_boot_key) and never presses CoCo keys, so the dismissing key cannot reach BASIC. MEASURED on hardware over serial: page up at 1.5 s, still waiting at 7.5 s when a key was sent, machine running 0.1 s later.]

[2026-09-27 DONE: confirmed on hardware by the user ("that's all working now"), board 1D21CC1CBE17D6F6: autorun.txt edited on screen and saved, the not-found page shown and dismissed with a key, and '@DISK SPACEWARP.DSK' on its own starting Spacewarp at power-on.]

summary: Per-game settings files: NAME.TXT beside a .bin, .ccc or .dsk, edited with Tab
description:
User direction 2026-09-28, replacing per-title palette files (PIZERO-55 closed): each game can have its own settings file, same format as settings.txt, including color_ lines. NAMING (user's call): ORBIT.BIN, ORBIT.CCC and ORBIT.DSK all use ORBIT.TXT beside the file.

Mounting a disk in a drive with 0-3 is not a launch and applies nothing. Tab on a highlighted entry in the F9 / F10 / F12 lists opens its NAME.TXT in the on-screen editor, from a template of commented examples if it does not exist. Saving the running game's file applies it at once; any other game's file applies when that game starts. A game named SETTINGS or AUTORUN would clash with the machine's own files, so Tab refuses it and says why.

summary: F1: an info page (board id, temperature, versions) that is also a CoCo-styled Markdown help reader
description:
User request 2026-09-28: F1 opens an INFO page, which also serves as the HELP system: context-sensitive help, the owner's manual, and any documents the user puts on the SD card, drawn by a Color Computer styled Markdown renderer.

1. F1 KEY. F1 (HID 0x3A) is unmapped today (src/main.cpp hid_keyboard_apply; overlay keys in src/overlay_keys.h, which claims only F9-F12 while closed). F1 pauses the machine and opens the page, as the F9-F12 lists do (same pause, audio silence and key capture, disk_overlay.cpp); F1 or ESC closes it. CAUTION: the CoCo 3 keyboard has real F1/F2 keys, and the Fruit Jam port reserved F1/F2 for the emulated machine for that reason. When CoCo 3 mode lands (PIZERO-133) F1 must either pass through there or move; decide then, note it in the docs.

2. INFO PAGE (first screen). The facts a person or a bug report needs: firmware version and git hash, build env; chip id, revision, unique board id (the flash id, already the USB serial number, e.g. 1D21CC1CBE17D6F6); system clock; chip temperature (analogReadTemp(), RP2350B ADC channel 8, no GPIO, a few degrees rough); last reset reason ([boot] chip_reset); uptime; free heap; SD card state; which ROMs loaded (Color/Extended/Disk BASIC); drives 0-3 and what is in them; the running program or cartridge and whether its NAME.TXT settings applied (PIZERO-154); USB devices, including the bound gamepad identity (PIZERO-13).

3. HELP, CONTEXT-SENSITIVE. F1 from an F9-F12 list explains that list's keys; from the text editor, the editor's keys and, for settings.txt, the settings; from a running machine, an overview (F keys, RUN button, autorun, settings). Built-in help text lives in firmware so it works with an empty card.

4. DOCUMENTS FROM THE CARD. Markdown files in a folder such as /coco/help/ (name to decide), including an owner's manual we ship (README/SETTINGS/AUTORUN material rewritten for the screen) and anything the owner adds. A list of documents like the F11 files list.

5. COCO-STYLED MARKDOWN RENDERER. Draws on the 32x16 text card (coco_boot_card_*, which already has inverse rows and cells) in the real 6847 font. A deliberately small subset: headings, paragraphs with word wrap at 32 columns, bullet and numbered lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code, horizontal rules, and links between documents ([text](other.md): arrows select, ENTER follows, Backspace goes back). Styling ideas to settle while building: headings as inverse bars or on colored SG4 semigraphic blocks (the 6847's 8 colors, as CoCo program title screens did); rules from semigraphic blocks; code in inverse. The 6847 has no lower case: text shows upper case, and lower case could show as inverse, as a real CoCo 2 does, which would also carry emphasis; decide which. Scrolling with Up/Down/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End as in the editor. Parser and layout as a pure header (like text_edit.h, dsk_catalog.h) with host tests: wrapping, every construct, a link table, and a long document fitting in memory (stream it from the card rather than load it whole; free heap ~114 KB).

SUGGESTED ORDER (close at ~80%, file the rest): F1 + info page first (small, useful for bug reports at once); then the renderer with built-in help; then card documents and links; context sensitivity last.
