summary: Gamepad: make Switch Pro mode work (the startup handshake), so the pad works whatever mode it is in
description:
Split from PIZERO-13 (done). The user's GameSir Tegenaria Lite keeps returning to its Switch Pro identity (057E:2009) on this board: after Home+Y, and it came back there after RUN restarts and a power-on until Android mode (Home+A) was set by hand. In that identity it sends one 64-byte reply (81 01 00 03 ...) and then nothing, because a Switch Pro controller waits for the host's USB startup handshake. Today src/gamepad.h marks it PAD_SILENT and the mount line says 'gamepad, no input in this mode'.

WORK: send the handshake from main.cpp at mount (or after the first 0x81 reply), over the interrupt OUT endpoint with tuh_hid_send_report, a path this port does not use yet. Known sequence (Linux hid-nintendo, SDL): 0x80 0x02 handshake, 0x80 0x03 baud, 0x80 0x02 again, 0x80 0x04 (USB only, no timeout), then subcommand 0x03 with argument 0x30 to select the full input report. Then decode report 0x30: buttons in bytes 3-5, left and right sticks as packed 12-bit values in bytes 6-11 (Y up is larger, so flip). Add PAD_SWITCH to gamepad.h with host tests, measure with the PAD_PROBE build, same mapping as the other identities.

WHY: the pad would work in any mode, and genuine Switch Pro controllers would work too. Same problem as FRUITJAM-91 in the Fruit Jam port, never done there because that board always got the DS4 identity. COMPLETION: in Switch mode, PRINT JOYSTK(0) sweeps and fire registers.

summary: Serial typing drops the first character of a line
description:
Seen 2026-09-28 while typing a test program over the USB serial port (serial_keyboard=on) during PIZERO-13. After NEW and a line 10, the line '20 GOTO 10' was stored as '0 GOTO 10': the leading 2 was lost. The same happened in the first attempt at 30 ms per character, and again at 80 ms per character with a 0.6 s pause after each Enter, so it is not simply typing too fast. Workaround used: start each line with a space, which BASIC ignores.

WHERE: src/main.cpp pump_keyboard() / next_keychar(). Serial characters are pressed for 3 frames (g_kb_hold) and then released with a 2-frame gap (g_kb_gap); autotype uses 5 and 4. Suspects, not yet tested: (1) Color BASIC is busy after Enter (tokenizing and inserting the line) and its key scan misses a 3-frame press, which would explain why only the first character after Enter goes; autotype's longer hold may be why autorun typing has not shown it; (2) the key-rollover logic in the ROM ignoring a press that arrives while it still considers the Enter key down. NOTE the PIZERO-13 joystick change made PIA0 PA7 follow the joystick comparator instead of always reading high; the ROM masks that bit in its key scan, but rule it out.

TEST: over serial, send NEW then 10 lines of '<n> PRINT <n>' with no leading space, then LIST, and count the lines stored with the wrong number. Try the autotype timings (5/4) for serial too, and a longer hold only for the character after a CR. COMPLETION: 100 lines typed over serial arrive intact.

[2026-09-30] Likely fixed by PIZERO-173: serial typing handing characters straight to BASIC's POLCAT routine, as upstream XRoar's auto_kbd.c does, instead of simulated key presses BASIC can miss while busy.

summary: USB: devices behind a multi-chip USB-C hub never mount (TinyUSB enumeration race)
description:
Split from PIZERO-54 (done). The user's multi-port USB-C hub is two hub chips chained (Terminus FE1.1s 1A40:0101 with a Genesys 05E3:0610 on its port 3) plus a built-in device on the first hub's port 4 (probably a card reader). Since PIZERO-54 both hubs mount (CFG_TUH_HUB=2 via scripts/patch_tinyusb.py), but a pad behind the second hub never does.

MECHANISM, from the pizero_usbdebug env's TinyUSB log: the pad gets its address (Set Address = 1); during the 2 ms post-SET_ADDRESS delay the first hub reports a connection change on port 4 and TinyUSB issues GET_PORT_STATUS on the shared control pipe; when the pad's next request (Get Device Descriptor) is due the pipe is busy, 'enum_delay_async 1627: ASSERT FAILED' (host/usbh.c, ENUM_AFTER_SET_ADDRESS_RECOVERY_DELAY), and the enumeration is abandoned with no retry. Present in Adafruit TinyUSB 3.7.7, the latest release as of 2026-09-28.

OPTIONS: (1) check upstream hathach/tinyusb master for a fix to hub status handling during enumeration, and whether the Arduino library can take it; (2) extend scripts/patch_tinyusb.py to retry (reschedule the delayed step when the control pipe is busy instead of asserting); (3) accept it and document 'use a simple hub'. A simple 4-port hub works (PIZERO-54). Low priority while simple hubs work.

summary: Setting joystick_swap: swap which pad stick drives the CoCo's right and left joysticks
description:
User request 2026-09-28. The pad mapping (PIZERO-13) puts the pad's LEFT stick (and D-pad) on the CoCo's RIGHT joystick, JOYSTK(0)/(1), the one most software reads, and the right stick on JOYSTK(2)/(3). Some players and games want it the other way. New settings.txt line joystick_swap = on | off (default off). On swaps the two CoCo ports as a whole: pad right stick -> JOYSTK(0)/(1) with the left-hand fire buttons (square, L1) on its fire bit, pad left stick and D-pad -> JOYSTK(2)/(3) with the right-hand buttons. Keeping each stick with the buttons on the other hand's side is deliberate: the steering thumb is busy, so the other hand fires. Because per-game files use the same format (PIZERO-154), a game can swap just for itself with a NAME.TXT. Applies live on save, like the other settings. WHERE: src/settings.h (field, parser, template, host tests in test/test_settings), src/main.cpp (the pad decode loop picks the destination port; [pad] telemetry reports CoCo port 0 after the swap; the [settings] log line), SETTINGS.md table, src/file_templates.h game template example.

CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-09-28 (user): played several games with joystick_swap = on through the hub with keyboard and pad; 'very helpful'. Nothing left over.

description:

summary: USB keyboard types what the keycaps say (not CoCo key positions); per-source key matrix
description:
User request 2026-09-28: the USB keyboard should use USB key mappings instead of emulating CoCo key positions, which is confusing. TODAY (positional): hid_table_init (src/main.cpp:331-357) maps key positions and passes Shift through, so Shift+2 gives '"', Shift+; gives '+', and no USB key reaches ':', '@', '*' or CLEAR; = [ ] \ ' ` Tab Home are unmapped. PLAN: (1) coco_machine gets one key mask per source (USB keyboard, serial/autotype, pad) ANDed in coco_pia0_preread_a, because today press/release_key is one bitmask where the last writer wins; (2) new pure header src/key_translate.h, host-tested: USB key + Shift -> ASCII via tek_ascii() (src/text_edit_keys.h:58-76, already the editor's table) -> CoCo key plus a forced SHIFT state via an extended ascii_to_dscan with the Color BASIC chords from upstream XRoar dkbd.c: [ = SHIFT+DOWN, ] = SHIFT+RIGHT, \ = SHIFT+CLEAR, _ = SHIFT+UP, ^ = UP ({ } | ~ ` press nothing; upstream's ~ = SHIFT+@ is PAUSE, not copied). Letters keep Shift passing through (CoCo's other case). Esc=BREAK, Backspace=LEFT, Home=CLEAR, Caps Lock=SHIFT+0. Physical Shift restored on release, as upstream hkbd.c:1460-1470. No positional option (user: drop it). Serial typing gains the same chords. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/let-s-try-the-6809-serene-penguin.md (approved 2026-09-28).

summary: Pad buttons press CoCo keys, set in settings.txt (pad_<button> = key), and dpad = arrows
description:
User request 2026-09-28: use all the pad's buttons; assigning key presses to pad buttons makes most sense. FINDINGS: each decoder in src/gamepad.h yields only two fire bits; unused are HID/Android top, buttons 3 and 6, byte 2 (buttons 9-15) and the triggers; XInput start/back/L3/R3/guide/top/triggers; DS4 top and byte 6 above R1. The CoCo 2 reads one fire button per joystick (PA0/PA1); the second button of two-button sticks is read only by a CoCo 3 (PA2/PA3; upstream coco3.c:1361 vs dragon.c:1341), and on a CoCo 2 those bits are keyboard rows, so a second fire would read as phantom keys; key mapping is the right tool for CoCo 2 games (note added to PIZERO-133). PLAN: pad_state gains a generic buttons mask (bottom, right, left, top, l1, r1, l2, r2, select, start, l3, r3, home), filled by each decoder; settings lines pad_<button> = left_fire | right_fire | none | a CoCo key name (A-Z, 0-9, SPACE, ENTER, BREAK, CLEAR, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, SHIFT, @ : ; , - . /), also in a game's NAME.TXT; dpad = joystick | arrows. Defaults keep today's fire buttons plus start=ENTER and top=SPACE. Keys go through the pad's own matrix source (PIZERO-163) and are released on unplug and while the overlay is open. Needs one PAD_PROBE=1 sweep to measure Android byte 2 and XInput start/back/L3/R3; DS4 bits per spec, unverified. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/let-s-try-the-6809-serene-penguin.md (approved 2026-09-28). 

SWEEP 2026-09-28 (new env pizero_padprobe, docs/BUILD.md), GameSir in Android mode: byte 2 = L2 01, R2 02, select 04, start 08, home 10, L3 20, R3 40; top face = byte 1 10; analog L2 in byte 9, R2 in byte 8. The M button is NOT a gamepad button: it sends a Print Screen keystroke (report ID 3, usage 0x46) from the pad's second interface, which the pad routing keeps off the keyboard path; a candidate trigger for PIZERO-165. The pad's Xbox-format report on interface 1 showed L3 40 / R3 80 in byte 2 and top 80 in byte 3, matching the standard layout. BUILT, awaiting hardware. gamepad.h split into decode (sticks, D-pad direction, a PAD_B_* button mask for 13 buttons; DS4 extra bits per its published layout, unverified) and pad_resolve (a struct pad_map from settings: fire, fire_right, none or a CoCo key per button; dpad = arrows presses arrow keys instead of moving the stick). Defaults reproduce the old fire buttons plus start = enter, top = space. main.cpp presses the pad's keys on the COCO_KEYS_PAD layer (PIZERO-163), redrawn only on change, cleared on unplug. key_translate.h gained kt_key_by_name/kt_key_name. Settings pad_<button> and dpad, also per game; the settings template now lists them (555 bytes: the overlay's and the test's 512-byte template buffers raised to 1 KB, and an 8-byte buffer that 'fire_right' overflowed was found and fixed before it shipped). 213 host tests. SETTINGS.md 'Gamepad buttons', README item 7. summary: Print Screen saves the screen as a PNG in /coco/screendumps on the SD card
description:
User idea 2026-09-28: pressing Print Screen writes what is on the screen to a PNG file in /coco/screendumps/ on the microSD card.

FACTS FOUND WHEN FILING: Print Screen is HID usage 0x46, unused today (not in overlay_keys.h or key_translate.h). The picture on the HDMI output is g_fb in src/main.cpp:208 (RGB565, FRAME_WIDTH x FRAME_HEIGHT = 320x240, with the CoCo's 256x192 active area centered; a second buffer in the double-buffered builds, main.cpp:213); it already includes artifact colors, a live GIME palette and any overlay card, so capturing g_fb captures exactly what the user sees. SD writes exist (coco_boot_save_text, src/coco_boot.cpp:290, FatFS).

DESIGN NOTES, to settle when worked: (1) capture the 256x192 active area (or the full 320x240 with border; decide), as an 8-bit indexed PNG: the screen uses few colors (16-color palette plus artifact colors), so build the palette while scanning, and fall back to 24-bit if more than 256 appear; 256x192 indexed is 48 KB of pixels. (2) PNG encoder as a pure, host-tested header: IHDR/PLTE/IDAT/IEND, CRC-32 and Adler-32, deflate with STORED blocks (no compression library, no big buffers; a few hundred bytes of code; files ~49 KB), streamed row by row to the file so no 48 KB buffer is needed. Host test: encode a pattern and check it decodes with a reference zlib/PNG reader (python3 in the test script, or known CRCs). (3) File names: /coco/screendumps/SCR0001.PNG counting up (scan for the next free number, create the folder if missing); maybe the running game's name (g_game_path, PIZERO-154) as a prefix. (4) Pause the machine while writing, as the overlay does (g_audio_paused silence, no emulation), since an SD write of ~50 KB takes a noticeable fraction of a second; show a brief confirmation (a status line on the card, or just the serial log) and the file name. (5) Also available from the serial console, so a screenshot can be taken without a keyboard. (6) The overlay card is part of g_fb, so Print Screen with a list open captures the list, which is useful for documentation.

COMPLETION: Print Screen at the BASIC prompt and in a game each produce a PNG on the card that opens on a computer and matches the screen, including artifact colors.

[2026-09-28 note from PIZERO-164] The GameSir pad's M button sends a Print Screen keystroke (HID usage 0x46, report ID 3) from its second interface. Consider accepting it as the screenshot trigger: a pad-only player could then take screenshots.

BUILT 2026-09-28. Decisions taken: the whole 320x240 screen (border and overlay included), files SCR0001.PNG counting up (no game-name prefix yet). src/png_write.h: streaming 8-bit indexed PNG, zlib with stored deflate blocks, nibble-table CRC-32, Adler-32; 5 host tests (round trip through a test decoder incl. the 320x240 two-block case, the standard IEND CRC), and an independent check: a generated 320x240 PNG decodes with Python zlib (all CRCs good) and reads as PNG 320x240 in macOS sips. coco_boot_screenshot(): creates /coco/screendumps, next free SCRnnnn.PNG, palette built from the screen, streamed through a 512-byte buffer from heap memory (freed after; the double-buffered build has no static RAM to spare), watchdog fed per block. Triggers in main.cpp: USB Print Screen (0x46, works with the overlay open), the GameSir M button (Print Screen from the pad's second interface), Ctrl-P over serial. Taken after a frame is drawn, sound paused, pacing restarted. MEASURED ON HARDWARE via Ctrl-P: SCR0001.PNG 77,131 bytes, 212 ms; SCR0002.PNG 77,134 bytes, 207 ms. HARDWARE CHECK LEFT: Print Screen key and the pad's M button; open a PNG from the card on a computer and compare with the screen (artifact colors, an overlay list).

CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-09-28 (user: 'screenshots work'). Closed at ~80%. Left for later if wanted: the running game's name as a file-name prefix, and an on-screen confirmation (today it is the serial [shot] line only).

[2026-09-28 follow-up, user: 'screen capture should work in the overlay too'] Print Screen and the pad's M button already did (confirmed: SCR0008 was taken with the FILES list open). Ctrl-P over serial did not, because the serial pump is paused under the overlay; the overlay branch of loop() now takes a Ctrl-P waiting at the front of the serial queue without consuming other characters. summary: font setting: classic, 6847t1, or our 6847t2 (default) with a real caret, underscore and { | } ~
description:
User request 2026-09-28: fix the emulated screen font so ^ looks like a caret, _ is not a left arrow, and curly braces exist; make the font set a setting with the older sets selectable; our own is the default, named 6847T2 for now.

FINDINGS: the machine renders every alpha character through the T1 font's upper block ((ch & 0x3F) | 0x40, coco_machine.cpp render_alpha_frame), i.e. as a plain 6847: codes 0-63 are the INVERSE characters (BASIC's 'lower case' is inverse capitals), ^ is an up arrow and _ a left arrow, and there is no { | } ~. Upstream mc6847.c:470-497 and dragon.c:1216: on a real CoCo 2B the 6847T1's EXT line is PIA1 PB bit 4 (GM0); with EXT on (POKE 65314,16) the T1 indexes its font by the full 7-bit code, which gives true lower case and { | } ~ (T1 glyphs $01-$1E), all drawn with INV set. Programs use codes 0-63 deliberately for inverse title bars and highlights, so always-on lower case (option (a)) would change how they look; the user named the font and did not choose, so the recommended (b) was built: 6847t2 = 6847t1 behavior plus a real caret for ^ (T1 glyph $00) and underscore for _ (T1 glyph $1F) at all times. BASIC cannot type { } from the keyboard even on a real CoCo 2B (no key chord); they display from CHR$ and programs.

SETTING: font = classic | 6847t1 | 6847t2 (default 6847t2), also per game (NAME.TXT). classic uses the original MC6847 font (lib/xroar_core/src/mc6847/font-6847.c, 768 bytes of flash, previously excluded from the build with a 1-byte stub in coco_machine.cpp).

User 2026-09-28: the choices are classic and 6847t1, with our 6847t2 the default. BUILT, awaiting hardware. vdg_pack.h vdg_alpha_glyph(ch, ext, font, &pair) (host-tested in test_vdg_pack, including checks against the real T1 glyph data: the underscore is one low bar, the caret sits in the top half, the braces mirror). coco_machine: font-6847.c now built (the 1-byte stub is gone), EXT taken from PIA1 PB bit 4 in coco_pia1b_postwrite, render_alpha_frame reads a 128-entry glyph/pair map rebuilt only when the font or EXT changes; coco_machine_set_font(). Setting font = classic | 6847t1 | 6847t2 in settings.h (tests), applied live, logged; SETTINGS.md row. POKE 65314,16 typed at the prompt was undone at once: BASIC wrote the register about 110 more times, back to 00, while reading keys and printing. Inside a running program the POKE held (pb_last=10, lower=1) until a PRINT, which resets it too (Extended BASIC returns the VDG to text mode when it prints). We run the real ROM, so a real CoCo 2B behaves the same: its true lower case only survives in programs that write screen memory directly. DECISION (user): add lowercase = on | off (default off). With font = 6847t2 and lowercase = on, codes 0-31 always show as true lower case and { | } ~ (vdg_lower_case() in vdg_pack.h, host-tested); off keeps inverse text authentic. 6847t1 stays exactly like the chip. summary: Keyboard auto-repeat, with a configurable rate or off
description:
User request 2026-09-28: auto-repeat on USB keyboard input, with the repeat rate configurable or turned off. TODAY: a held USB key is simply held down in the CoCo's key matrix (PIZERO-163 key layers), so any repeat is whatever the running program does; Color BASIC itself does not auto-repeat a held key. The on-screen editor already has its own repeat (TEK_REPEAT_DELAY 24 frames, TEK_REPEAT_RATE 3, src/text_edit_keys.h), which shows the timing approach. DESIGN NOTES: repeat by releasing and re-pressing the held key in the USB layer (coco_machine_release_key_src / press_key_src) on a frame timer, for the newest held key only (as PC keyboards do), and only for keys that type characters or move the cursor, never SHIFT or BREAK. A release must stay down for at least as long as BASIC's keyboard scan needs to see it (see PIZERO-158, where a 3-frame press was missed after Enter). Games read held keys directly from the matrix; repeat would make them see flickering presses, which is why it must be switchable, per game too (NAME.TXT). SETTINGS: key_repeat = off | on (or a rate), key_repeat_delay = milliseconds, key_repeat_rate = per second; exact names to decide. Default: probably off, so games behave as on a real CoCo, and on in settings.txt for typing; decide with the user.

USER DECISION 2026-09-28: default ON ('by default every improvement we make is default'). BUILT, awaiting hardware. key_translate.h kt_repeat(): the newest held USB key, after key_repeat_delay, is released for KT_REPEAT_GAP=2 frames every period (60/key_repeat_rate frames, at least KT_REPEAT_MIN=5, so 12 a second at most) and pressed again; BREAK never repeats; a new press restarts the delay; older held keys stay down. kt_keys omits the newest key during the gap. main.cpp hid_key_repeat() runs once a frame beside pump_keyboard. Settings key_repeat (on), key_repeat_delay (500 ms, 100-2000), key_repeat_rate (10, 1-30); 5 host tests for the timer plus settings tests. SETTINGS.md and README. HARDWARE CHECK: hold a letter at the OK prompt: one, then after half a second a steady stream; hold Backspace (LEFT) to delete a run; key_repeat = off in settings.txt stops it; a game that reads held keys, with key_repeat = off in its NAME.TXT if it flickers.

CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-09-28 (user: 'key repeat is sweet'). Closed at ~80%: not yet tried against a game that reads held keys directly; if one flickers, key_repeat = off in its NAME.TXT is the documented answer.

summary: The pad drives the overlay: Home toggles it, D-pad moves, A selects, B goes back
description:
User request 2026-09-28: the controller's HOME button toggles the overlay, the D-pad navigates it, A selects and B goes back, so the machine can be used with the pad alone.

DESIGN: the overlay (disk_overlay.cpp, overlay_keys.h) is driven by HID keyboard codes with its own edge detection, so the pad produces the same codes and main.cpp merges them with the keyboard's before calling disk_overlay_key (feeding the two separately would make its edge detection see alternating reports). Pure mapping pad_nav_codes() in gamepad.h, host-tested. Closed: Home = the F key of the list last shown (opens it). Open: Home and B (right face) = ESC, A (bottom face) = ENTER, D-pad = arrows (up/down move, left/right switch lists), L1/R1 = PgUp/PgDn, X (left face) = TAB (edit the entry's settings, PIZERO-154). Home stops being mappable (pad_home removed). While the overlay is open the pad presses no CoCo keys or fire; buttons held when it closes stay inert until released, so launching with A or leaving with B is not also a fire press (the pad's version of FRUITJAM-68). NOT covered: assigning a disk to drives 0-3 from the pad (keyboard only), and typing in the text editor.

BUILT 2026-09-28, awaiting hardware. gamepad.h pad_nav_codes() (host-tested, codes checked against overlay_keys.h); PAD_BUTTON_NAMES has no 'home', so pad_home is now an unknown setting and pad_resolve never maps Home. main.cpp: overlay_feed() merges the keyboard's held keys (g_kb_codes) with the pad's (g_pad_nav) before disk_overlay_key, and on close resyncs both (kt_resync, and g_pad_inert/g_pad_dpad_inert keep held pad controls inert until let go). Home: opens via disk_overlay_open() (the last list shown); closes only once let go since opening, else the opening press would close it at once. While open the pad sends the machine centered sticks, no fire, no keys. Held D-pad gets the overlay's own key repeat. SETTINGS.md, README item 7. HARDWARE CHECK: Home opens the list last shown; D-pad up/down moves (held repeats), left/right switch lists; A starts a program/cartridge/disk without a stray fire in the game; B closes; Home closes; X opens the highlighted game's settings file; the keyboard still drives the overlay with the pad plugged in.

CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-09-28 (user: 'that's working pretty well'; telemetry showed the machine paused under an overlay opened from the pad). Closed at ~80%: individual checks (X for settings, D-pad repeat, no stray fire after launching with A) were not reported one by one. Not covered by design: drives 0-3 and typing in the editor, which need the keyboard.

summary: GIME timer: confirm which revision's reload quirk to emulate (it sets the tempo of timer music)
description: Split from PIZERO-62 (done: the GIME-compatible timer works on hardware, 2026-09-28). The GIME's timer counts a reload of N as N+2 on the 1986 part and N+1 on the 1987 part (per ~/github/coco coco-guides/coco3-intro.md; PIZERO-62 first recorded this backwards and corrected it on 2026-09-18). The build option GIME_PERIOD_BIAS defaults to 2, the 1986 part. Music and timing loops written for one revision run slightly fast or slow on the other, so the choice sets the tempo of timer-driven music. TO SETTLE: time a known CoCo 3 timer program (a music player with a published tempo, or a test that counts timer interrupts per second against the 60 Hz frame) on this board, against the same program on desktop XRoar set to each GIME revision, or a recording from a real CoCo 3 of known revision. If the difference is inaudible in practice, record that and keep 2. A setting (gime_revision = 1986 | 1987) is an option if both matter; under the project rule the default would be whichever real programs expect most. Also recorded in PIZERO-62 and kept deliberately: a reload of 0 stops the timer here, where real hardware re-asserts the interrupt at once (the 'Arkanoid sound bug'), because an every-tick timer would wedge the emulator.

summary: Attract mode: when idle, cycle through a playlist of demos and games until someone touches a control
description:
User request 2026-09-28, for showing the CoCo Zero at Tandy Assembly (Saturday 2026-10-03): an attract mode. When nobody has touched a control for a few minutes, the machine starts cycling through a playlist of demos and games, each for a while, until someone presses a key or a pad button, which stops the cycle and leaves them in whatever is running (or returns to where they were). Classic booth behaviour: a board on a table keeps showing something worth watching.

WHAT EXISTS TO BUILD ON: the launcher (perform_launch in src/main.cpp, PIZERO-81d) already cold-starts a .bin, .ccc or .dsk by path, applying its per-game settings (settings_for_game, PIZERO-154); autorun.txt already names what to start at power-on; all input arrives in one place (hid_keyboard_apply, the pad path in tuh_hid_report_received_cb, serial pump), so 'last activity' is one timestamp updated there; the frame counter g_frame_count gives the time.

DESIGN SKETCH, to settle when worked: (1) the playlist: a text file, e.g. /coco/attract.txt, one program, cartridge or disk per line with an optional time in seconds, in the autorun.txt style (reuse its parsing and name resolution, and report missing names the same way, PIZERO-152). (2) settings: attract = on | off, attract_idle (minutes before it starts), attract_time (default seconds per entry); by the project rule an improvement is on by default, but with no attract.txt there is nothing to cycle, so it only acts once a playlist exists. (3) any key, pad button or stick movement stops cycling immediately and does NOT reach the game as input (the same 'inert until released' rule as the overlay close, PIZERO-169), so a visitor's first press just takes over. (4) never while an overlay list or the editor is open; never while serial typing is active. (5) the watchdog restart after a freeze (PIZERO-33) should land back in attract mode, which autorun.txt pointing at the first entry already gives. (6) optionally a one-line caption on screen when an entry starts (its name), using the card; only if cheap.

TESTS: the idle timer and playlist stepping as a pure header with host tests (next entry, wrap-around, per-entry time, the input that stops it). HARDWARE: leave the board alone with a 3-entry playlist and watch it cycle; press a pad button mid-entry and check the game keeps running without receiving that press.

TIMING: only worth building before the show if the display (PIZERO-99), freeze (PIZERO-168) and hub-replug (PIZERO-51) checks come out clean by midweek.

summary: Type { } | ~ and backtick (and paste faster) by handing characters to BASIC's keyboard routine, as XRoar does
description:
User question 2026-09-30: with the USB keyboard translation, why can't { } | ~ and backtick be typed, when the 6847t2 font can show them? Because Color BASIC reads keys through its own decoder from the CoCo's key matrix, and no CoCo key or chord produces those characters; the keyboard translation (src/key_translate.h, PIZERO-163) can only press CoCo keys. Lower-case mode only shifts letters.

THE PROVEN WAY: upstream XRoar's automatic typing (src/auto_kbd.c in ~/github/xroar) does not press keys at all. It sets a breakpoint on the ROM's keyboard routine POLCAT and, when BASIC asks for a key, hands it the character directly. XRoar's symbol table (src/symtab.c) gives POLCAT per ROM: $A1C1 for Color BASIC (symtab.c:144), $A1CB in another (symtab.c:238), with $A000 being the POLCAT vector (symtab.c:66). No ROM file is modified.

PLAN: (1) in the emulation loop, a cheap check when the CPU reaches the POLCAT entry (for example in coco_mem_cycle when the opcode fetch address matches, or a PC compare in mc6809_run), and only while a character is queued; (2) when one is queued, return it as POLCAT does (A = the character, the 'key ready' flag set, then RTS), exactly as auto_kbd.c's handler; (3) queue the characters the matrix cannot make ({ } | ~ `), from key_translate.h, so the keyboard otherwise keeps pressing real keys (games read the matrix and must keep working); (4) route serial typing and autotype through the same queue, which should fix PIZERO-158 (serial dropping the first character of a line) and make pasting fast; (5) a table of POLCAT addresses per supported ROM, identified by a checksum of bas12.rom / extbas11.rom at boot, and the old key-press path whenever the ROM is unknown.

LIMITS: works wherever a program reads keys through BASIC's routine (the prompt, INPUT, INKEY$); a program that scans the keyboard hardware itself still sees only real key presses. The characters then display through the 6847t2 font with lowercase on (both defaults; PIZERO-166).

TESTS: the queue and the ROM table as pure headers with host tests; on hardware, type { } at the prompt and see them, paste a long program over serial and count dropped characters (PIZERO-158's test).

TIMING: after the Tandy Assembly show (2026-10-03); not a pre-show change.

summary: Benchmark the CoCo 3 (GIME) video modes on the board, including a 640-wide display path
description: User 2026-10-01: 'can we start benchmarking coco3 video modes xroar supports?' and 'we should evaluate for a 640-wide display path for performance. we may be surprised.' Independent of the CPU-speed track (PIZERO-129 to 131): that decides whether a CoCo 3 can RUN fast enough; this measures whether the board can DRAW its modes. WHAT TO MEASURE, per mode, on hardware: (1) core 0's cost to turn a frame of GIME video memory into display pixels (XRoar's tcc1014.c produces each scanline as 6-bit GIME color values, up to 640 per line, through its render_line delegate; ~/github/xroar pin a2d31903); (2) core 1's cost to scan out a 640-wide picture, which today's 320x240 RGB565 framebuffer (doubled to 640x480) cannot do: candidates are an indexed framebuffer (640x240 at 8, 4 or 2 bits per pixel: 150, 75 or 38 KB) with palette lookup during the TMDS encode, or per-line rendering straight into the line buffer (no full framebuffer); (3) the RAM each needs against today's ~127 KB free (75.7 percent used); (4) whether streaming audio islands still fit alongside. MODE MATRIX (from tcc1014.c): text at 32, 40, 64 and 80 columns; graphics at 256, 320, 512 and 640 pixels wide with 2, 4 or 16 colors; 192, 200 and 225 lines. At least: 320x225x16, 640x225x4, 640x225x2, 256x192x16, 80x24 text and 40x24 text. HOW: a bench env (like the old pizero_bench, retired in PIZERO-150) that fills video memory with a pattern per mode, renders with a GIME-compatible renderer (vendored from tcc1014.c, or a minimal equivalent of its render path) and prints per-frame microseconds for render and encode; no 6809 needed. Results into docs/measurements/ and docs/coco3-feasibility.md. WHY IT MATTERS: the same 640-wide path unlocks CoCo 3 80-column and 640-wide modes (PIZERO-134), native 80-column text (PIZERO-90), the F18A's 80 columns (PIZERO-16) and an MC6845 80-column card (PIZERO-176). The user expects it may be surprisingly feasible; measure before deciding. STEP 1 STARTED 2026-10-02: env pizero_videobench (-DVIDEO_BENCH) times libdvi's encoders per scanline on core 0 with interrupts off while core 1 scans out (src/main.cpp, VIDEO_BENCH block). Getting the 640-wide encoders to link needed two libdvi fixes: lib/libdvi/tmds_encode.h now gives every assembly encoder C linkage (only the two loops in use had it, so tmds_fullres_*, tmds_palette_* and tmds_encode_1bpp/2bpp were unlinkable from C++), and the fullres/palette loops and their tables do not fit in scratch X/Y beside the core stacks (X over by 1480 bytes, Y by 768), so -DTMDS_FULLRES_IN_SRAM=1 moves them to main SRAM for the bench. A real 640 path must solve that placement (smaller stacks, or one copy in X for core 1 only). Product, fallback and wavmeas firmware verified byte-identical with these changes. STEP 1 RESULTS 2026-10-02 (board 1D21CC1CBE17D6F6, 252 MHz, core 0 with interrupts off while core 1 scans out; ns per encoded line, budget 63,500 because each line is shown twice, minus core 1's audio island work): libdvi software: today 320 doubled 16bpp 25,200; 640 distinct 16bpp 55,600; 640 palette 16 or 256 colors 57,900; 640 1bpp 5,950; 640 2bpp 6,600. Placement and options, measured and dropped: fullres loops in scratch Y instead of SRAM 54,400 (-2%), palette loop in scratch 57,400 (-1%); TMDS_FULLRES_NO_DC_BALANCE 46,800 fullres / 53,800 palette; plus NO_INTERP_SAVE 45,500. None leaves comfortable room for audio. THE FINDING: the RP2350 has a hardware TMDS encoder in SIO (one per core, SIO_TMDS_CTRL/WDATA/PEEK_DOUBLE_Ln/POP_DOUBLE_Ln) that libdvi predates. One write of two RGB565 pixels, one read per lane gives two symbols in libdvi's two-symbols-per-word format, DC-balanced by the hardware. Bench (src/main.cpp, bench_hw_*): today's 320 doubled 12,600 (half of today's software cost); 640 distinct 16bpp 15,700 to 17,200; 640 from 8-bit palette indices via an RGB565 lookup 23,700. A decode self-check (bench_hw_check) decodes all 1,920 symbols of a 640 line back to pixels: 0 errors, so symbol order and lane order match libdvi. NOT YET SHOWN: a picture from the hardware encoder on a real display (the bench never sends its symbols). NEXT: (a) a 640-wide display path on core 1 using the SIO encoder, needing a 640-wide framebuffer or a per-line render (RAM: a 640x240 16bpp buffer is 300 KB, too much beside audio; 8-bit index lines rendered per line, or 4bpp 150 KB/2bpp, are the options); (b) step 2, GIME per-mode render cost on core 0. Even without 640, switching today's encode to the SIO encoder would halve core 1's video encode time. SHIPPED TO MAIN 2026-10-02 (for the Tandy Assembly release, user: 'switch today's picture to the hardware encoder ... make sure we can switch using the settings.txt'): today's 320-doubled picture now encodes on the SIO hardware encoder by default. lib/libdvi/tmds_encode.cpp tmds_encode_16bpp_sio_doubled (scratch X, 112 bytes; PIX2_NOSHIFT doubling, CLEAR_BALANCE each line, all three lanes in one pass), chosen per scanline in _dvi_prepare_scanline_16bpp by the global dvi_sio_tmds_encode (lib/libdvi/dvi.cpp). settings.txt video_encoder = hardware (default, improvements on) | software (libdvi's tables); applied in settings_apply, so the on-screen editor switches it live. F1 INFO shows VIDEO HARDWARE/SOFTWARE ENCODER. Checkpoint before this: lightweight tag checkpoint/pre-sio-tmds. First boot on board 1D21CC1CBE17D6F6: 60 fps, settings log video_encoder=hardware. AWAITING the user's eyes on a real display, in both settings. CLOSED 2026-10-02 at the useful substance, confirmed on hardware by the user: 'picture looks ok. makes sounds. f1 says hardware. flipping the settings, it seems no different. info says software. flipping it back says hardware again. works predictably so far.' Delivered: the encoder benchmark (pizero_videobench), the finding that the RP2350 SIO encoder makes a 640-wide color line affordable (about 16 us of a 63.5 us budget), and today's picture moved onto it with a settings.txt switch. Remainder filed: PIZERO-178 (GIME per-mode render cost on core 0, the original step 2) and PIZERO-179 (a 640-wide display path on the SIO encoder; RAM is now the constraint, not encode time).

summary: MC6845 CRTC: an 80-column card for the CoCo Zero, for demos and developers
description: User 2026-10-01: 'i've been considering supporting the MC6845 CRTC' and, if the 640-wide path holds, 'it's worth doing the mc6845 emulation in context just for the demos if nothing else. CoCo Zero is like a little playground for developers, and our limits do not always need to be practical if they are within reach.' WHAT A 6845 IS: a CRT controller, a timing chip: it generates sync and the video-memory addresses but draws nothing itself. A card built on it supplies its own video RAM and character ROM. In the CoCo world that means an 80-column card (Radio Shack's Word-Pak is believed to be 6845-based; verify, and find its I/O address and character ROM before building). Elsewhere: IBM MDA/CGA, BBC Micro, Amstrad CPC, Apple II 80-column cards. Upstream XRoar has no 6845 emulation, so this is new code. DEPENDS ON the 640-wide display path (PIZERO-175): 80 readable columns need 640 pixels across, and today's framebuffer is 320 wide. SCOPE: the 6845 register file (screen geometry, cursor), an 80x24 text card with its own RAM and a character ROM we can ship (our own font, like the 6847T2, not a copyrighted ROM), and enough compatibility for existing CoCo 80-column software if any can be found; homebrew demos otherwise. DEFAULT: on, as an extension; off under 'classic' (PIZERO-177).

summary: A 'classic' setting: one line that turns every extension off for an authentic CoCo 2

The CoCo Zero's default is the extended machine (project rule in CLAUDE.md: improvements are on by default). Today each extension has its own setting, so getting a stock CoCo 2 means turning many off. PLAN: a setting such as `machine = classic | extended` (name to settle; extended is the default) that, when classic, sets every extension to its authentic value in one go: sn76489 off, gime_palette and gime_timer off, font = classic (or 6847t1), lowercase off, key_repeat off, and future extensions off too (TMS9918A PIZERO-16, MC6845 PIZERO-176). Individual settings after it in the file still override it, and it works per game in NAME.TXT (PIZERO-154), so one game can be classic. Host-tested in test_settings; documented in SETTINGS.md. [2026-10-22 DONE by PIZERO-242: machine = coco2 is the one-line authentic CoCo 2 (sn76489, gime_palette, gime_timer, lowercase off, font classic), works per game in NAME.TXT, and individual lines still override it; confirmed on hardware. Deliberately different from this plan: key_repeat is not turned off, because the user decided profiles govern only the emulated hardware, not host conveniences. Future extensions (TMS9918A, MC6845) should default off in coco2 and coco3 via settings_profile() in src/settings.h.]

summary: Benchmark XRoar's GIME scanline render per CoCo 3 video mode on core 0
description: Remainder of PIZERO-175 (its step 2). PIZERO-175 measured the display side: libdvi software encode vs the RP2350 SIO hardware TMDS encoder (bench env pizero_videobench, src/main.cpp VIDEO_BENCH block). This is the render side: time XRoar's GIME renderer (lib/xroar_core tcc1014.c render_scanline, around line 1290) for each mode it supports, on the board, per scanline and per frame. Modes: graphics HRES byte widths 16/20/32/40/64/80/128/160 at CRES 1/2/4 bpp (2/4/16 colors), and text at 32/40/64/80 columns with and without attributes. Report each against core 0's frame budget (pizero_stream_60 currently uses 76.2% at CoCo 2 1x; see docs/cpu-speed.md) and say which modes fit at 320 wide and which need the 640-wide path (PIZERO-179). Can extend pizero_videobench rather than add an env. Note the port suppresses XRoar's per-scanline render (SUPPRESS_RENDER_SCANLINE) and renders the VDG by frame (coco_machine_render_frame), so the GIME renderer must be driven directly with synthetic register state.

summary: A 640-wide display path on the RP2350's hardware TMDS encoder
description: Remainder of PIZERO-175. The SIO hardware encoder (lib/libdvi/tmds_encode.cpp tmds_encode_16bpp_sio_doubled, default since d509181) encodes a 640-wide line of distinct RGB565 pixels in about 15.7 to 17.2 us and one from 8-bit palette indices in 23.7 us, against a 63.5 us budget per encoded line (each line is shown twice), measured in pizero_videobench with a decode self-check of 0 errors. libdvi's software fullres encoders take 55.6 to 57.9 us and are not viable. So encode time is no longer the limit; RAM is. A 640x240 RGB565 framebuffer is 300 KB and does not fit beside the audio island buffers (product RAM is 75.7%). Options to evaluate: (a) core 1 renders one line at a time from a compact source (8-bit palette indices, or the emulated chip's own VRAM), (b) a 4 bpp 640x240 framebuffer (75 KB) or 8 bpp (150 KB) with a palette lookup in the encode loop, (c) 2 bpp/1 bpp for 80-column text (libdvi's tmds_encode_1bpp is 6 us a line in software). Needed for GIME 640/512-wide modes, 80-column text, the MC6845 card (PIZERO-176) and possibly the TMS9918A (PIZERO-16, 256 wide, fits 320 today). Start with a fixed 640-wide test pattern on screen, behind a build flag, before wiring any emulated chip to it. 2026-10-20: option (b) at 8 bpp is built and shipped for the CoCo 3 by PIZERO-134 (dvi_static_framebuf_main_pal8 + tmds_encode_pal8_sio, a 640x240 index framebuffer in the RGB565 buffer's RAM). What is left here is using it for the other 640-wide chips: the MC6845 card (PIZERO-176), 80-column text on the CoCo 2 side (PIZERO-90), and whether the CoCo 2 build should move to the same path.

description: User 2026-10-02: 'a setting file will always be rendered for editing with it's keys in alphabetical order. with comments at the top. we don't have to do anything beyond that for now, but the file is effectively opened "clean" each time we edit.' settings_tidy in src/settings.h (pure, host-tested): comment lines ('#') first in their order, a blank line, then setting lines sorted by name, case ignored, stable for repeated names (the last still wins when parsed). summary: Autorun as one boot-time feature: autorun = on | off, reset_button = basic | autorun, a Space or BREAK tap cancels it
description: User 2026-10-02: 'i don't know what it does and the name is not intuitive enough to guess', then 'yes go with reset_button, it's better and i understand what it's doing better now'. The setting (PIZERO-116) decides what the board's RUN button, a hardware reset on the RP2350's RUN pin, does: basic (default) restarts to a clean BASIC prompt ignoring autorun.txt; power_on restarts like a power cycle, autorun included. The old name described the mechanism, and 'run' reads as the BASIC command. Done: src/settings.h field reset_to_basic, parsed from reset_button = basic | power_on; run_skips_autorun = on | off still accepted so existing cards keep working; template, [settings] log line, the AUTORUN SKIPPED boot page ('THE RESET (RUN) BUTTON WAS PRESSED'), SETTINGS.md, AUTORUN.md and docs/kit.md updated. Host tests in test/test_settings cover both names. EXTENDED 2026-10-02, user: 'i would like to have a simple option called "autorun" that is on or off. let's have the values for reset_button be basic and autorun so that they are clear and consistent with that. one more thing, holding down space or break during boot should disable autorun.' Done: autorun = on | off (default on; off ignores autorun.txt at every start, logged '[autorun] off in settings.txt'); reset_button values are basic | autorun (power_on, never pushed, is gone; run_skips_autorun still accepted). Space (HID 0x2C), Esc (0x29, the CoCo BREAK) or Pause (0x48) held at boot skips autorun with the AUTORUN SKIPPED page and its own body (MSG_KEYSKIP_*). The check (src/main.cpp, after the RUN check) services the USB host until the keyboard has reported, or 150 ms after it mounted, or 2.5 s after the host started with no keyboard; no wait when nothing is connected (usbdiag_connected false 300 ms after the host started), and none when there is no autorun to skip. Measured on board 1D21CC1CBE17D6F6: a keyboard behind a hub, after a gamepad, mounts 1.4 s after the host starts; the check waited 1.3 s. So an autorun boot with a keyboard now starts about 1.3 s later than before. Not done: the gamepad cannot skip autorun. 2026-10-02, user: 'get rid of run_skips_autorun.' The old name is no longer accepted (it reports as an unknown setting and is ignored); the test asserts SET_UNKNOWN. 2026-10-02, user: 'if we have reset_button=autorun and autorun=off it should autorun i would expect.' So autorun = off governs power-on only; a RUN reset follows reset_button (autorun runs it even with autorun = off). Space/BREAK held still skips in every case. src/main.cpp run_wants_autorun; SETTINGS.md and AUTORUN.md say so. HARDWARE FINDINGS 2026-10-02 (user's Keychron K2, vid 3434 pid 0430, behind a hub): holding Space never worked. The keyboard sends no report for a key already down when it connects, and our first boot check watched only 150 ms. A GET_REPORT (input) right after mount was added: it answered with an empty report in most tries, once with Space (00 00 2C ...), so it helps only sometimes. Taps are reported from 45 ms after mount; the user's taps were missed only when they fell outside the watch window, and with no cue it was impossible to know when to tap. Now: once the keyboard mounts, an AUTORUN page (MSG_ARWAIT_*: 'PRESS SPACE OR BREAK TO SKIP IT AND START AT THE BASIC PROMPT.') is shown and boot watches for KB_WATCH_MS = 1000 ms; a Space/Esc/Pause in a report, or in the GET_REPORT answer, skips autorun. The AUTORUN SKIPPED page is then held 2 s with boot_hold (not dismissable), because the user's next tap was closing it before it could be read ('sometimes i get a message but i can't read it'). Cost: an autorun boot with a keyboard attached takes about 1 s longer than before this issue. Docs say tap, not hold. REVISED 2026-10-02, user: 'i don't really want the page. i just want to autorun to be aborted if i type a space.' The AUTORUN prompt page is gone (it was also mostly lost to the display re-locking after a RUN restart: seen for half a second with a 2 s window). Boot now watches for KB_WATCH_MS = 600 ms after the keyboard mounts, with nothing on screen; tapping from switch-on is the documented way. The AUTORUN SKIPPED page and its 2 s hold stay. REVISED again, user: 'we don't need the whole autorun skipped page that has too much text to read anyways. just get rid of that. i never asked for it.' A Space/BREAK skip now goes straight to BASIC with no page; MSG_KEYSKIP_* and boot_hold removed. The RUN-button skip page from PIZERO-116 is unchanged. And the RUN-button AUTORUN SKIPPED page from PIZERO-116 is removed too (user: 'i do not want those pages. they are stupid.'): MSG_RUNSKIP_* gone, RUN with reset_button = basic goes straight to BASIC. No skip of any kind shows a page now; each is logged on serial. CLOSED: confirmed on hardware by the user 2026-10-02 ('yes all good now'): autorun = off starts at BASIC, RUN with reset_button = autorun autoruns, a Space tap at start skips to BASIC, no pages. Not done: the gamepad cannot skip autorun, and a held key goes unseen on keyboards like the Keychron K2 (tap instead). REOPENED 2026-10-02: closed too early. User: 'autorun is one feature. When you boot, if it's enabled for the default disk (disk 0) and you haven't typed space at least once, it's going to run. Doesn't matter how you boot, it's a boot-time feature that runs as soon as BASIC is loaded. the reset_button feature, enables/disables it temporarily as part of the RUN button's function.' And: 'either first .bin or first bas file, like it always has' and 'autorun.txt should not even be consulted when autorun is turned off.' The closed version did not match: autorun = off only stopped autorun.txt, ENTER on a disk in F12 always typed RUN, and the default disk never autoran. REBUILT (src/main.cpp): autorun_on = autorun && !(RUN restart && reset_button = basic). Off: autorun.txt is not read; Disk BASIC with drive 0's disk, nothing typed. On: autorun.txt's typed lines, else drive 0's first program (disk_run_command: first .BIN or .BAS), whatever disk is in drive 0. ENTER on a disk in F12 (perform_launch) follows autorun the same way. The boot-time keyboard wait, GET_REPORT and their globals are gone, so no boot delay. Not cancellable: @DIRECT and @CART, which start before the keyboard is up. Hardware 2026-10-02 (serial log): power-on with autorun on typed autorun.txt's lines; ENTER on tiny-agent with its own settings file saying autorun = off stopped at BASIC, and after it said on, typed LOADM"RAIN":EXEC; RUN with reset_button = basic did not read autorun.txt; a Space tap after ENTER on SWORD cancelled it ('[autorun] cancelled'). User: 'this is fine for now. let's keep testing.' Open question left with the user: whether autorun should count in a game's own settings file. CLOSED 2026-10-02 on the user's word: '182 is good to close.' Left open as a question, not filed: whether autorun should count in a game's own settings file.

summary: Investigate SD 1.1 / no-name cards that never answer the SPI start-up
description: See PIZERO-184 for the cards and the evidence: a batch of Lerdisk 2 GB cards (ID '??asdfg', manufacturer 0x05, SD spec 1.1) fails f_mount with FR_NOT_READY on every try, while the user's other card works in the same slot. The SD driver (carlk3 no-OS-FatFS-SD-SDIO-SPI-RPi-Pico, .pio/libdeps/.../src/sd_driver/SPI/sd_card_spi.c) does support version 1.x cards (it logs 'Card Initialized: Version 1.x Card'), so card type alone should not explain it. Plan: a debug build (a real env, per docs/BUILD.md) with the driver's DBG_PRINTF on, to log each command and reply in the start-up (CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41 or CMD1, CMD58) for one of these cards; then try what is cheap: a slower init clock than the default, more ACMD41 retries or a longer timeout, extra clock cycles with CS high before CMD0, and a longer power-up delay. Settle whether these cards can be made to work or are simply SPI-incapable, and record the answer in PIZERO-184's kit note. Only worth doing if cheap small cards matter for the kits; not for the 2026-10-03 show. src/main.cpp mount_sd() retries f_mount five times 200 ms apart; the pins are in src/hw_config.c (SCK 30, MOSI 31, MISO 40, CS 43, card detect 22, about 12.5 MHz).

summary: F8 cycles the artifact colors and saves the choice for the running game
description: User 2026-10-02: 'i'd like to make F9 toggle artifact modes and save the new setting in the coresponding settings file for the running program/cart/disk', then 'F8, and save to settings.txt when nothing launched'. (F9 already opens the programs list.) Plan: F8 while the machine runs (overlay closed) cycles artifact_colors on -> swapped -> off -> on, applies it at once (coco_machine_set_artifact), and writes 'artifact_colors = <value>' into the running game's own settings file (NAME.TXT beside it, from g_game_path via settings_game_path), creating it if needed, or into /coco/settings.txt when nothing was launched. The line is replaced where it is (the last one with that name, since the last wins), else appended; the rest of the file is kept as written. Pure helper in src/settings.h with host tests; the SD write happens in loop(), not in the USB callback. No page on screen; a serial line says what was saved where. README controls table and the SETTINGS.md artifact_colors row mention F8. summary: Retrospective of the show-prep work (2026-10-01 and 10-02)

summary: Refine autorun's scope around its purpose: what a machine does after it powers up
description: User 2026-10-02, after PIZERO-182 closed: 'autorun is for what a machine does after it has powered up. it allows demos to be reset easily and to start themselves. it wasn't really built to be a general purpose automation for all of the disks installed, though it could be perceived that way. it's definitely an idea that needs refinement, but that won't be done today.' As shipped (PIZERO-182, 183): autorun = on runs autorun.txt's typed lines, else drive 0's first program, on every boot: power-on, the reset button with reset_button = autorun, and ENTER on a disk in F12 (perform_launch in src/main.cpp follows g_settings.autorun). A Space or BREAK tap before the typing starts cancels it; autorun = off does not read autorun.txt. Questions for the refinement: should ENTER on a disk in F12 be governed by autorun at all, or always launch (it did before PIZERO-182); should the default disk with no autorun.txt autorun (it did not before PIZERO-182); should `autorun` be allowed in a game's own settings file (one game's file turning it off confused a test); and how a demo setup is best expressed (a card that starts a demo and returns to it on reset). Start from the purpose and agree a rules table before code (docs/show-prep-retrospective.md, lesson 1). Not before the 2026-10-03 show.

summary: Flash-and-QC process for a batch of boards: flash, board serial, sticker photo, QC log
description:
User 2026-10-03 (show day): 'we need to flash a bunch of boards. about 14 i think. can you help me setup a process by which we flash the board, retrieve it's board serial number, photograph the inspection sticker sn and record that information in a QC log?' Camera: the user chose 'Achtung Mini Camera' (ffmpeg avfoundation; tested, about two seconds of frames before the shot so focus settles). scripts/qc_flash.py: per board, wait for BOOTSEL (or send a running board there with the 1200-baud touch), picotool load -v -x the release firmware.uf2, wait for the board's USB serial device (VID 2E8A) and take its USB serial number (the board ID the F1 INFO page shows), read 8 s of boot log and pass when 'DVI up' and 'USB host up' appear, photograph the inspection sticker, OCR it with tesseract (--psm 11; candidates are 6+ letter/digit runs with a digit) and have the operator confirm or type the number, then append to qc/qc-log.csv (unit, time, board_serial, sticker_sn, firmware, firmware_sha256, flash, boot, photo, boot_log, notes) with qc/photos/NN-serial.jpg and qc/logs/NN-serial.txt. Refuses a -dirty firmware build unless --allow-dirty; warns on a board already logged.

summary: NitrOS-9 hangs after loading OS9Boot: fix the $FF40 drive-select decode, trace the FDC
description: User 2026-10-03: a NitrOS-9 disk (/coco/dsk/zork1.dsk, header fixed by the user) now boots with DOS but hangs right after loading OS9Boot. The console shows no [dsk] errors; the emulator keeps running (fps=60, freezes=0), so the guest is stuck, most likely waiting on the FDC. Found while reading the FDC: fdc_io_write in lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp treats $FF40 bits 0-3 as one-hot drive select, but bit 3 is MOTOR ON and drive 3 is bit 6 (upstream ~/github/xroar/src/rsdos.c:291-301: bit 0/1/2 -> drives 0-2, else bit 6 -> drive 3, else drive 0). A latch write of motor-on without a drive bit selects the empty drive 3 here and reads come back NOT READY with nothing logged. DO: decode the latch as upstream does; add a pizero_fdctrace env (-DFDC_TRACE) that logs every latch change and FDC command ([fdc] lines: latch, drive, command, track, sector, resulting status, CPU PC) and the CPU PC once a second, so the hang can be located. DONE WHEN: the trace shows where NitrOS-9 stops, and either it boots or the remaining cause is filed. Other FDC gaps this may surface (no side select or tracks past 34, writes report write-protect, Type III commands stubbed, Step without direction does nothing) get their own issues. FINDINGS 2026-10-03 (pizero_fdctrace on hardware): ZORK1.DSK is 161280 bytes and a 6809 NitrOS-9 Level 1 boot track (REL, Krn, KrnP2, Init, Boot; no 6309 opcodes). DOS reads track 34 sectors 1-18 cleanly; after that the FDC receives no command at all, so the hang is not in the FDC. The latch fix is in but did not change the symptom. The boot loops: 'NITROS9 BOOT' flashes repeatedly and the PC keeps returning to REL's relocated copy loop and the kernel's RAM clear. Remainder filed as PIZERO-191. CLOSED 2026-10-08: the latch decode and pizero_fdctrace shipped; the hang itself was PIZERO-191's three bugs, fixed in 31872bc and confirmed on hardware (NitrOS-9 reaches OS9:).

summary: NitrOS-9 Level 1 boot loops: the kernel re-enters REL before loading OS9Boot
description: Remainder of PIZERO-190. With ZORK1.DSK (NitrOS-9 6809 Level 1), DOS loads track 34 and REL relocates it to $EE00, prints NITROS9 BOOT and enters Krn's cold start at $EE8C. Something then sends execution back into REL ($EE00-$EE7A), so the message flashes forever and the FDC sees no further command (OS9Boot is never read). Lead, unconfirmed: Krn's first system call, F$Link of Init via SWI2 at $EF46, fails and its LBCS returns to $EE8C; a fault in SWI2/IRQ vectoring in all-RAM mode (vectors $FFF0-$FFFF fetched from BASIC ROM via the case 7 I/O map, through the $0100 RAM vectors Krn copies in) would loop exactly this way. The GIME_TIMER/GIME_PALETTE extensions are also on in the product build and worth ruling out. NEXT: flash pizero_fdctrace, type DOS with the serial logger connected; the [pctrace] dump (armed at $EE8C, fired on re-entry to REL) lists the jumps that lead back, which should name the failing instruction. DONE WHEN: NitrOS-9 boots to its shell on hardware, or the cause is pinned and filed. STATE 2026-10-04 (end of session): the board was left running pizero_fdctrace with the jump recorder (commit ac9120d); its dump was not captured before the board was disconnected, so start by flashing pizero_fdctrace (pio run -e pizero_fdctrace -t upload), connecting a serial logger from boot, and typing DOS. Do not trigger a dump on PC < $0100: Color BASIC runs CHRGET at $009F and RAM hooks at $01xx, so that fires before DOS (tried, wasted one capture). The [fdc] io log of $FF90-$FFDF is capped at 200 writes and BASIC's startup SAM writes use them all before DOS; raise the cap or arm it at DOS if GIME writes need checking. Flash the product build (pio run -t upload) when done. ROOT CAUSES 2026-10-08, found and fixed in the cocozero emulator (pizero_fdctrace_uart, autorun.txt typing DOS): (1) REL clears $FF03 (60 Hz IRQ off) and enters all-RAM mode; PIZERO-31's fix forced PIA0 CRB bit 0 back on every frame (coco_machine_run_cycles), so the next field-sync IRQ vectored through $010C into Disk BASIC's handler at $D8AF, now RAM, and the CPU slid through memory until it re-entered REL (the flashing NITROS9 BOOT). (2) PIZERO-31's real cause: the firmware pulsed CART for every cartridge ROM including Disk BASIC, so after the cold start Color BASIC's autostart FIRQ ($A0F6) re-initialised the PIAs (60 Hz IRQ off, after Extended BASIC had turned it on at $80A3) and restarted Disk BASIC at $C000. Fix: no CART pulse for a ROM with 'DK' at $C000 (coco_machine_install_cart_sized sets cart_autostart), and the forced CRB bit removed. (3) The FDC ended every read on track 0 with status $04 (TRACK00), which after a Type II command is LOST DATA, so NitrOS-9's Boot (BITB #$9C at $FD4F) failed every LSN 0 read and recalibrated forever; reads now end with $00. Verified in the emulator: NitrOS-9 boots to OS9: (screen read via [scr]); Disk BASIC idles with CRB=$35 and PRINT TIMER advances 211, 330, 450; the Mega-Bug cartridge still autostarts; 230 host tests pass. NEEDS: hardware confirmation with the product build (ZORK1.DSK to the OS9: prompt; PLAY and the cursor blink in Disk BASIC; a cartridge autostarts). CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-10-08 with the product build (pizero_stream_60, commit 31872bc): ZORK1.DSK boots to the OS9: prompt; serial log clean (60 fps, no freezes, no [dsk] errors). The Disk BASIC TIMER and cartridge autostart regression checks were not run on hardware; filed as PIZERO-192.

summary: Hardware regression check for the PIZERO-191 PIA/CART changes: Disk BASIC TIMER and cursor blink, cartridge autostart
description: PIZERO-191 (commit 31872bc) removed the per-frame forcing of PIA0 CRB bit 0 that PIZERO-31 added, and stopped pulsing CART for a ROM with 'DK' at $C000 (Disk BASIC). Both were verified in the cocozero emulator but only the NitrOS-9 boot was confirmed on hardware (2026-10-08). CHECK on the board with the product build: (1) fresh boot into Disk BASIC: the cursor blinks and PRINT TIMER advances between presses (the 60 Hz IRQ stays on after Extended BASIC enables it at $80A3); (2) PLAY produces sound; (3) a game cartridge (Mega-Bug) still autostarts via CART; (4) a Disk BASIC disk other than NitrOS-9 still loads (LOADM / RUN). DONE WHEN: all four pass on hardware, or a failure is pinned and filed. If (1) fails, PIZERO-31's symptom (no TIMER, no cursor blink) is back and the fix needs a cause that is not the forced CRB bit. CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-10-08: Disk BASIC cursor blinks and TIMER advances; Mega-Bug autostarts. PLAY and a plain Disk BASIC LOADM were not tried explicitly, but PIZERO-191's NitrOS-9 boot exercises the same FDC read path and the IRQ is proven on by TIMER, so closed at this.

summary: Create a blank, formatted .DSK from the F12 disk list (N key)
description: Writable drives (PIZERO-66) need a disk to write to, and the board has no way to make one. DO: N in the DISKS list creates the next free /coco/dsk/NEWnn.DSK (NEW01, NEW02, ...), 161280 bytes of $FF, which is exactly what Disk BASIC's DSKINI leaves (every FAT granule free, every directory entry unused), written to a .tmp and renamed so a power cut never leaves a short image under the real name; the list rescans and lands on the new disk so 0-3 mounts it. The directory is created if missing. Watchdog fed during the ~160 KB write. NOT DONE HERE, filed if wanted: typing a name on the board (rename on a PC for now); 40-track or double-sided blanks; an OS-9 formatted blank (NitrOS-9's format command can do that itself on a blank). DONE WHEN: on hardware, N makes NEW01.DSK, it mounts in drive 1, DIR shows an empty disk with 68 granules free, SAVE to it works and the file is sound in desktop XRoar. 2026-10-09: NEW01.DSK auto-naming worked on hardware (426 ms to create; a SAVE to it worked), but the user wants the name typed at creation. N now opens a one-line prompt in the status row (NAME: _): letters, digits, - and _, upper-cased, up to 16 characters, Backspace, Enter creates NAME.DSK in /coco/dsk (refused if it exists), Esc cancels. The list rescans and lands on the new disk. NEEDS: hardware confirmation of the prompt. CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-10-09: the prompt made MYDISK.DSK (410 ms), it mounted, and a SAVE to it wrote and synced. Closed.

summary: Hardware checks left over from writable drives: power cycle after SAVE, W lock gives ?WP ERROR, NitrOS-9 write, desktop XRoar opens the image
description: PIZERO-66 closed on SAVE/LOAD working within a session (and after the 1.5 s idle sync, which the log shows). CHECK on the board: (1) SAVE a program, wait 2 s for the [dsk] synced line, power cycle, LOAD it back; (2) in the disk list press W on a mounted disk (drives.txt gains 'ro'), close the overlay, SAVE: expect ?WP ERROR, then W again and the SAVE works; (3) boot ZORK1.DSK to OS9:, create a file (build /d0/hello, a line, a blank line), list it, power cycle, list it again; (4) copy MYDISK.DSK to a PC and open it in desktop XRoar, LOAD the saved program. If (3) fails look first at the side-select and track-range limits in coco_boot.cpp (dsk_offset) and the Type III stubs in coco_machine.cpp. DONE WHEN: all four pass or a failure is filed. FINDINGS 2026-10-09: the NitrOS-9 write test stalled on the disk, not the firmware. ZORK1.DSK's OS9Boot holds IOMan, RBF, rb1773, DD, SCF, VTIO, CoVDG, Term, Clock, Clock2, SysGo, Shell: its only disk descriptor is /DD (no /D0), and CMDS holds only shell_21 and infocom, so 'dir', 'build' and 'list' give ERROR #216 (command not found) and any /d0 path gives ERROR #221 (the kernel tries to load a 'D0' descriptor module). The pizero_fdctrace build now prints a checksum per sector read ([dsk] rd ... sum=), and every sector OS-9 read (LSN 0, 2, 3, 68, 69, 104-132) matched the image, so reads are byte-exact. The game runs as INFOCOM /DD/GAMES/INFOCOM/ZORK1.Z3 and its 'save' to /dd/game1 is the write test; not yet done. Caps lock under OS-9 is CLEAR+0 (Home+0), see PIZERO-197. OS-9 WRITE DONE 2026-10-09 (found in the trace log afterwards): Zork's 'save' as ZORKSTUF (no path, so the data directory, /dd root) wrote 93 sectors: the allocation map (LSN 1), the root directory FD and data, then the file from track 26 sector 17 on; max 2.1 ms, mean 0.8 ms, sync 6 ms; Zork printed OK. Remaining: power cycle, start the game again and 'restore' ZORKSTUF. CLOSED 2026-10-09: restore of ZORKSTUF after a power cycle worked on hardware, which proves the write, the idle sync and persistence end to end under NitrOS-9's RBF. Two checks not run, filed as PIZERO-200: the W lock giving ?WP ERROR, and desktop XRoar opening a disk written here.

summary: About a second of audio underruns right after a launch from the F12 overlay
description: Seen in the serial log 2026-10-09 while testing PIZERO-66, on every launch from the overlay: the [aud] line after the launch reports prod=16609-35660/s against want=48000 with under=1303-4421/s and short=2.7-9.2%, then the next second is clean (prod=48069, under=0). Not from the disk writes (none in those seconds). Likely the launch itself on core 0: disk11.rom load (8 KB), settings files, cold reset, and the 180-frame autotype warm-up, all inside one frame's budget, or the audio ring left empty while the overlay paused it (g_audio_paused) and refilling at 1x. DO: time perform_launch, and check whether the ring is primed before audio resumes; a launch should be silent, not a crackle. DONE WHEN: the [aud] line after a launch shows under=0.

summary: Rename a .DSK from the F12 disk list (R key)
description: Follows PIZERO-193 (N makes a named blank disk). R on the highlighted disk opens the same one-line prompt pre-filled with its name (without .DSK); Enter renames the file in place (same directory, .DSK kept), Esc cancels, a name already taken is refused. A disk that is in a drive is ejected from every drive holding it, renamed, and remounted in the same drives with its write-protect tab kept, so the open FatFs handle and drives.txt stay right. The prompt now keeps the case typed (the editor font shows lower case) and allows up to 24 characters, the width the status row has. DONE WHEN: on hardware, R renames an unmounted disk and a mounted one, the list shows the new name, the drive still reads it, and drives.txt names the new file. CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-10-09: renamed an unmounted disk and the one in drive 0, which was remounted under the new name and still read. Closed (commit f6f23c2).

summary: Caps Lock under NitrOS-9: a capslock setting choosing the chord (SHIFT-0 for BASIC, CTRL-0 i.e. CLEAR+0 for OS-9)
description: Found 2026-10-09 while testing NitrOS-9 writes: Caps Lock had no effect under OS-9. The USB Caps Lock key is translated to the CoCo chord SHIFT+0 (key_translate.h, as upstream XRoar's dkbd does), which is Color BASIC's case toggle. NitrOS-9's Level 1 console driver (level1/modules/vtio.asm, key table entry '0 0 capslock' = plain, SHIFT, CTRL) toggles caps on CTRL-0, where CTRL is the CLEAR key on a CoCo 1/2 (and @ is ALT); SHIFT-0 just types '0'. Its default on a non-CoCo2B build is V.Caps=$FF: unshifted letters upper case, SHIFT+letter lower, CTRL-0 flips that. So today the user holds Home (our CLEAR) and presses 0. DO: a settings.txt / NAME.TXT key, capslock = basic | os9 (default basic), so a NitrOS-9 disk's own NAME.TXT makes the Caps Lock key send CLEAR+0; and mention CLEAR+0 in the README's OS-9 notes. Also consider the serial keyboard (kt_chord types letters unshifted, so upper case under OS-9's default). DONE WHEN: with capslock=os9 in ZORK1.TXT, Caps Lock toggles case at the OS9: prompt.

summary: pizero_fdctrace_uart crashes at boot in the cocozero emulator since the PIZERO-66 coco_machine change; the product build runs
description: Found 2026-10-09 while trying to reproduce the NitrOS-9 ERROR #221 offline. In ~/github/cocozero-emulator (binary of 2026-10-08, commit 578d94e) run headless with --turbo 6, the trace build from HEAD prints nothing on UART0 and core 0 sits at 0x1000BC40, which is the spin in __NVIC_SystemReset reached from Hardfault_HandlerC or capture_assert; the product build (pizero_stream_60) from the same tree runs and reaches BASIC. Bisected in a scratch export of 31872bc (the last trace build that ran there): copying in only the new lib/coco_machine/src/coco_machine.cpp and .h reproduces the crash; adding three padding fields of the same size to the old struct does not. The new code paths (write sector, idle hook) cannot execute at boot, so it looks like the emulator mis-executing some instruction the new build happens to place on a boot path. The emulator pokes fixed firmware addresses only when injecting keys (keyboard.rs KB_MATRIX_ADDR, soc.rs HID_REPORT_ADDR/TRAMP_ADDR), so that is not it in headless mode. DO: find the faulting instruction (an instruction trace or fault log in the emulator would do it; that is a change in the emulator's own project) or move the trace output so the crash address can be read. Until then the trace build runs on hardware only. Staging for the emulator: a folder with coco/roms (bas12, extbas11, disk11), coco/dsk, coco/drives.txt written exactly as the firmware writes it ('1 = ' with the trailing space) and coco/autorun.txt; pass it with --sd. autorun text now accepts '~' as a one-second pause, so a line can follow a DOS boot.

summary: Build a NitrOS-9 Level 1 working disk (dir, list, build, copy, format) for the card
description:
Idea from 2026-10-09: the only OS-9 disk on hand is a Zork game disk with /DD only and no utilities, so nothing can be listed or created from its prompt. Make a proper NitrOS-9 Level 1 CoCo 2 disk from a release image on the Mac: standard CMDS, descriptors /d0 /d1 /dd, and put it in /coco/dsk. It is the natural test bed for the write path (build, copy, del, format of a blank made with N) and can mount the Zork disk in drive 1. Deferred by the user ('fine for now'). 2026-10-09 started. Source: the user's CoCo SDC collection has NITROS9/nos9l1.dsk, a 31 MB SDC hard-disk image of NitrOS-9 3.3.0 6809 Level 1 that carries the whole module set (NITROS9/6809L1/MODULES) and 80 commands. Plan: scripts/mkos9disk.py reads that image and writes a 35-track single-sided floppy the distribution's own way (SCRIPTS/mb.floppy): boot track rel+krn+krnp2+init+boot_1773_6ms on track 34, OS9Boot from BOOTLISTS/standard.bl with the _35s descriptors (DD, D0, D1, D2) in place of _40d, sysgo, CMDS trimmed to fit (no basic09, runb, asm, disasm, dcheck, ded, minted, sdc, sdcdriver, boot_sdc, dw, tuneport, megaread, grfdrv), SYS/errmsg, the official Startup. Verified on the Mac in desktop XRoar 1.10 headless (the board is soaking) with a test copy whose startup runs dir, free, makdir, copy and list into a log file on the disk. BUILT 2026-10-09: scripts/mkos9disk.py (reads the source image read-only, writes LSN0, the allocation map, directories with contiguous files, OS9Boot as one run named in LSN0, and the boot track on track 34; --list prints a disk's tree). Output ~/Desktop/coco/dsk/NOS9L1.DSK: 66 commands, boot file 13,122 bytes, boot track 4,067 bytes, 210 sectors (52 KB) free. VERIFIED in desktop XRoar 1.10 headless (coco2bus, rsdos, DOS typed) with test copies whose startup logged to the disk: boots; dir /d0 and dir /dd list the root; free reports 630 sectors; makdir, copy and list write files byte-identical to their source (3,649-byte errmsg); dir -e lists all 66 commands; mdir shows the 3.3.0 modules including D0, D1, D2, DD and the pipe modules; devs shows DD and D0 on rb1773 at $FF40. Test-script lessons: in the OS-9 shell '>>' redirects error output (no append), file names cannot contain '-', and a script needs '-x' to continue past an error. Plain dir into a file or pipe drops lines (it cannot read a screen width); dir -e is clean. NEEDS: copy NOS9L1.DSK to the card after the PIZERO-168 soak, boot it on the board with DOS, answer the time prompt, and run dir, free and a write (build or copy).

[2026-10-12 DONE on hardware: the bench board C58D06257AE30E85 (product build 904e014, which also has PIZERO-131's direct RAM path, so this doubles as its all-RAM-mode check) booted NOS9L1.DSK from the card with DOS; the user was asked to run dir, free and a write (build) and reported "everything is ok so far".]

summary: Two leftover checks on writable drives: W lock gives ?WP ERROR; desktop XRoar reads a disk written here
description: Left over from PIZERO-194 when it closed on the NitrOS-9 save/restore. (1) In the F12 disk list press W on a mounted disk (drives.txt gains 'ro'), close the overlay, SAVE in Disk BASIC: expect ?WP ERROR; W again, SAVE works. (2) Copy Disk2.DSK (or any disk SAVEd to here) to a PC and open it in desktop XRoar; LOAD the program. DONE WHEN both pass.

summary: Soak log on the SD card with real timestamps, so a soak runs plugged into a power supply with no laptop
description:
User 2026-10-09: the PIZERO-168 soak should not need the Mac; log to the card, and timestamp with the RTC if that is cheap. FACTS: the RP2350 has no RTC block and this board no RTC chip or backup cell; it has the power manager's always-on timer (pico/aon_timer.h), free-running while powered, kept across a watchdog reboot, zero at power-on. The carlk3 SD library already stamps files from it (my_rtc.c get_fattime -> aon_timer_get_time) and saves the last time in .uninitialized_data across resets; we never start the timer, so files get epoch dates (the PIZERO-64 note). Reading it is a register read. DO: (1) clock seed at boot when the timer is not running: the newest modification time among /coco/settings.txt, drives.txt, autorun.txt and the newest /coco/log file, plus one minute, since the Mac wrote those with real time and the board's own files then keep it monotonic; log '[clock] set from card: <iso> (approximate)'; F1 INFO shows the date and time. (2) settings.txt key soak_log = on|off (default off: a diagnostic, not an improvement to the machine). (3) With it on, each boot opens the next /coco/log/soak-NNN.txt and writes a header: firmware version, env, power-on or watchdog reboot, the carried freeze tally and phase, the clock source.
